title.en: Volume 431 Biographies 190: Confucian Scholars 1 - Nie Chongyi, Xing Bing, Sun Shi, Wang Zhaosu, Kong Wei, Kong Yi, Cui Song and son: Lu, Yin Zhuo, Tian Min, Xin Wenyue, Li Jue, Cui Yizheng and younger brother: Woquan, Li Zhicai
title.raw: 卷四百三十一 列傳第一百九十 儒林一 聶崇義 邢昺 孫奭 王昭素 孔維 孔宜 崔頌子:曥 尹拙 田敏 辛文悅 李覺 崔頤正弟:偓佺 李之才 Volume 431 Biographies 190: Confucian Scholars 1 - Nie Chongyi, Xing Bing, Sun Shi, Wang Zhaosu, Kong Wei, Kong Yi, Cui Song and son: Lu, Yin Zhuo, Tian Min, Xin Wenyue, Li Jue, Cui Yizheng and younger brother: Woquan, Li Zhicai

sentences.zh: 聶崇義

translations.literal: Nie Chongyi
translations.idiomatic: Nie Chongyi

sentences.zh: 聶崇義，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Nie Chongyi was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Chongyi was from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少舉《三禮》，善《禮》學，通經旨。

translations.literal: In his youth he was selected in the Three Rites, was skilled in ritual studies, and thoroughly understood the purport of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he qualified in the Three Rites, excelled in ritual learning, and had a firm grasp of the meaning of the classics.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，累官至國子《禮記》博士，校定《公羊春秋》，刊板於國學。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou period of Han he successively reached the post of Doctor of the Book of Rites at the Imperial University, collated the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and had blocks carved at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Later Han's Qianyou reign he rose to become university lecturer on the Book of Rites, collated the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and had it printed from blocks at the national academy.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，累遷國子司業兼太常博士。

translations.literal: In the Xiande period of Zhou he was repeatedly promoted to Vice-Director of the Imperial University and concurrently Doctor of the Grand Secretariat of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Zhou during the Xiande era he was promoted repeatedly until he served as vice-director of the imperial university and concurrently as a ritual specialist at court.

sentences.zh: 先是，世宗以郊廟祭器止由有司相承製造，年代浸久，無所規式，乃命崇義檢討摹畫以聞。

translations.literal: Previously, Shizong found that the sacrificial vessels for suburban and ancestral temples were manufactured only by officials passing them down through successive generations; as years gradually lengthened there were no standards or models, and he therefore ordered Chongyi to examine, investigate, copy, and draw them and report.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Shizong had noted that suburban and temple ritual vessels were made solely by officials handing designs down through the generations; over time no standard models survived, so he ordered Chongyi to research the antiquities, draw them up, and submit his findings.

sentences.zh: 四年，崇義上之，乃命有司別造焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Chongyi submitted [his work]; the emperor then ordered the appropriate officials to manufacture [vessels] separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Chongyi presented his drawings, and the court ordered the relevant offices to cast new vessels accordingly.

sentences.zh: 五年，將禘於太廟，言事者以宗廟無祧室，不當行禘祫之禮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when a di sacrifice was to be held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, those who addressed affairs stated that because the ancestral temple had no shrine for distant forebears, the di and xia rites should not be performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, as a di sacrifice at the imperial ancestral temple was planned, memorialists argued that without a distant-ancestor shrine the temple could not properly conduct the di and xia succession rites.

sentences.zh: 崇義援引故事上言，其略曰：「魏明帝以景初三年正月上仙，至五年二月祫祭，明年又禘，自茲後以五年為禘。

translations.literal: Chongyi cited precedents and submitted a memorial, the gist of which was: "Emperor Ming of Wei ascended to immortality in the first month of the third year of Jingchu; in the second month of the fifth year the xia sacrifice was performed, and the next year the di sacrifice was held; thereafter the di sacrifice was held every five years.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi cited precedent and memorialized the throne, in summary as follows: "Emperor Ming of Wei died in the first month of Jingchu 3; the xia rite was performed in the second month of year 5, and the di rite the year after; from then on the di sacrifice was held every five years.

sentences.zh: 且魏以武帝為太祖，至明帝始三帝，未有毀主而行禘祫。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Wei Emperor Wu was taken as the founding ancestor; by the time of Emperor Ming there were only three emperors, and there were no tablets yet removed to the distant shrine when the di and xia rites were performed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wei took Emperor Wu as its founding ancestor; by Emperor Ming's time there were only three reigns on the throne, and the di and xia rites were still performed before any distant-ancestor tablets had been set up.

sentences.zh: 其證一也。

translations.literal: This is the first proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first precedent.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉六年，祠部定十月三日大祠，其太學博士議云：案禘祫之禮，三年一，五年再。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, the Department of Sacrifices fixed the great sacrifice on the third day of the tenth month; the doctors of the Imperial University deliberated, saying: According to the rites of di and xia, one occurs every three years and both occur every five years.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 6 of Emperor Wen of Song, the sacrifices office set the great rite for the third day of the tenth month; university scholars argued that the di and xia ceremonies come once every three years and twice every five.

sentences.zh: 宋高祖至文帝裁亦三帝，未有毀主而行禘祫。

translations.literal: From Emperor Gaozu of Song to Emperor Wen there were likewise only three emperors, and the di and xia rites were performed though no tablets had yet been removed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song founder to Emperor Wen there were likewise only three sovereigns on the throne, yet the di and xia rites were still performed before any distant tablets had been established.

sentences.zh: 其證二也。

translations.literal: This is the second proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second precedent.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝用謝廣議，三年一禘，五年一祫，謂之大祭，禘祭以夏，祫祭以冬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang adopted the proposal of Xie Guang: a di sacrifice every three years and a xia sacrifice every five years, called the great sacrifices; the di sacrifice in summer and the xia sacrifice in winter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang followed Xie Guang's proposal: a di sacrifice every three years and a xia every five, termed the great sacrifices—the di in summer and the xia in winter.

sentences.zh: 且梁武乃受命之君，裁追尊四朝而行禘祫，則知祭者是追養之道，以時移節變，孝子感而思親，故薦以首時，祭以仲月，間以禘祫，序以昭穆，乃禮之經也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Liang Wu was a ruler who had received the Mandate; he had only just posthumously honored four generations when he performed the di and xia rites—thus one knows that sacrifice is the way of continuing to nurture the departed. As seasons shift and festivals change, a filial son is moved and thinks of his kin; therefore offerings are made at the start of the season, regular sacrifices in the middle month, and di and xia at intervals, arranged by senior and junior lines—this is the constant of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Liang Wu was a ruler who had received Heaven's mandate; he had only just raised four generations of forebears when he performed the di and xia rites—showing that sacrifice is the way of continuing to honor the dead. As seasons turn and festivals change, a filial son is stirred to remember his kin; hence offerings at the season's opening, regular sacrifices in the middle month, and di and xia at set intervals, ordered by senior and junior lines—this is ritual's constant principle.

sentences.zh: 非關宗廟備與未備。

translations.literal: It has nothing to do with whether the ancestral temple is complete or incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: It does not depend on whether the ancestral temple is fully equipped or not.

sentences.zh: 其證三也。

translations.literal: This is the third proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third precedent.

sentences.zh: 」終從崇義之議。

translations.literal: " In the end [the court] followed Chongyi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end the court adopted Chongyi's view.

sentences.zh: 未幾，世宗詔崇義參定郊廟祭玉，又詔翰林學士竇儼統領之。

translations.literal: Before long, Shizong ordered Chongyi to assist in fixing the jade objects for suburban and temple sacrifices, and also ordered Hanlin Academician Dou Yan to take overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Shizong ordered Chongyi to help determine the ritual jades for suburban and temple sacrifices, and appointed Hanlin academician Dou Yan to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 崇義因取《三禮圖》再加考正，建隆三年四月表上之，儼為序。

translations.literal: Chongyi thereupon took the Illustrations of the Three Rites and subjected them to further examination and correction; in the fourth month of the third year of Jianlong he submitted them in a memorial, and Yan wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi then took the Illustrations of the Three Rites and revised them further; in the fourth month of Jianlong 3 he submitted them by memorial, with Yan supplying the preface.

sentences.zh: 太祖覽而嘉之，詔曰：「禮器禮圖，相承傳用，浸曆年祀，寧免差違。

translations.literal: Taizu read and praised it, issuing an edict that said: "Ritual vessels and ritual diagrams have been handed down and used in succession; as years and sacrifices gradually pass, how can discrepancies be avoided?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu read the work and commended it, decreeing: "Ritual vessels and ritual diagrams have been handed down through the ages; over countless years of sacrifice, errors were bound to creep in.

sentences.zh: 聶崇義典事國庠，服膺儒業，討尋故實，刊正疑訛，奉職效官，有足嘉者。

translations.literal: Nie Chongyi manages affairs at the National University, devotes himself to Confucian learning, investigates ancient facts, corrects doubtful errors, and in performing his duties and serving his office is worthy of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Chongyi serves at the imperial university, is devoted to Confucian learning, has traced antiquity and corrected doubtful errors, and in discharging his office has done work well worth praising.

sentences.zh: 崇義宜量與酬獎。

translations.literal: Chongyi should be given rewards in appropriate measure.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi should receive a suitable reward.

sentences.zh: 所進《三禮圖》，宜令太子詹事尹拙集儒學三五人更同參議，所冀精詳。

translations.literal: The submitted Illustrations of the Three Rites should be ordered to have Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Yin Zhuo gather three to five Confucian scholars to deliberate together further, in hope of thoroughness and detail.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Illustrations of the Three Rites he has presented, the heir apparent's grand mentor Yin Zhuo should gather three to five Confucian scholars to review them jointly, so that the result may be as precise as possible.

sentences.zh: 苟有異同，善為商確。

translations.literal: If there are differences, let them be well discussed and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Where opinions differ, let them be thoroughly debated and resolved.

sentences.zh: 」五月，賜崇義紫袍、犀帶、銀器、繒帛以獎之。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month he bestowed on Chongyi a purple robe, rhinoceros-horn belt, silver vessels, and silks as a reward.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month he rewarded Chongyi with a purple robe, a rhinoceros-horn belt, silver vessels, and silks.

sentences.zh: 拙多所駁正，崇義復引經以釋之，悉以下工部尚書竇儀，俾之裁定。

translations.literal: Zhuo made many corrections and refutations; Chongyi again cited the classics to explain, and all [matters] were referred down to Minister of Works Dou Yi to have him decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo raised many objections; Chongyi answered by citing the classics again, and the whole dispute was referred to Minister of Works Dou Yi for a final ruling.

sentences.zh: 儀上奏曰：「伏以聖人制禮，垂之無窮，儒者據經，所傳或異，年祀浸遠，圖繪缺然。

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial saying: "I humbly consider that when the sages established ritual, they bequeathed it without end; Confucians rely on the classics, yet what is transmitted may differ; as years and sacrifices gradually recede, illustrations are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized the throne: "Your subject reflects that the sages established ritual to endure forever, yet scholars who follow the classics often transmit differing views; as the years pass, the illustrated records have fallen into disrepair.

sentences.zh: 踳駁彌深，丹青靡據。

translations.literal: Contradictions grow ever deeper, and there is no basis in painted records.
translations.idiomatic: Contradictions grow ever deeper, and the painted records offer no firm ground.

sentences.zh: 聶崇義研求師說，耽味禮經，較於舊圖，良有新意。

translations.literal: Nie Chongyi has investigated the teachings of his masters and steeped himself in the ritual classics; compared with the old illustrations, his work has genuine new insight.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Chongyi has studied his teachers' doctrines and immersed himself in the ritual classics; compared with the old diagrams, his revisions contain real merit.

sentences.zh: 尹拙爰承製旨，能罄所聞。

translations.literal: Yin Zhuo received the imperial charge and was able to exhaust what he had heard.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhuo carried out the imperial commission and set forth everything he knew.

sentences.zh: 尹拙駁議及聶崇義答義各四卷，臣再加詳閱，隨而裁置，率用增損，列於注釋，共分為十五卷以聞。

translations.literal: Yin Zhuo's refutations and Nie Chongyi's replies, four scrolls each; your subject again examined them in detail, then decided and arranged them, generally adopting additions and deletions and setting them out in annotations, altogether divided into fifteen scrolls to report.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhuo's objections and Nie Chongyi's replies, four scrolls each—I have reviewed them again in detail, ruled on each point, generally adopting additions and deletions, and arranged them in annotated form in fifteen scrolls for Your Majesty's review.

sentences.zh: 」詔頒行之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered it promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the work promulgated.

sentences.zh: 拙、崇義復陳祭玉鼎釜異同之說，詔下中書省集議。

translations.literal: Zhuo and Chongyi again presented their differing views on sacrificial jades, tripods, and cauldrons; an edict referred the matter to the Secretariat for collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo and Chongyi again submitted their opposing views on ritual jades, tripods, and cauldrons; the emperor ordered the Secretariat to convene a joint discussion.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書張昭等奏議曰：

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhao and others submitted a deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhao and others memorialized with their opinion:

sentences.zh: 按聶崇義稱：祭天蒼璧九寸圓好，祭地黃琮八寸無好，圭、璋、琥並長九寸。

translations.literal: According to what Nie Chongyi states: for sacrificing to Heaven, the azure bi is nine inches with a round central perforation; for sacrificing to Earth, the yellow cong is eight inches without a perforation; the gui, zhang, and hu are each nine inches long.
translations.idiomatic: According to Nie Chongyi: the azure bi for Heaven sacrifice is nine inches with a round central hole; the yellow cong for Earth sacrifice is eight inches without a hole; the gui, zhang, and hu are each nine inches long.

sentences.zh: 自言周顯德三年與田敏等按《周官》玉人之職及阮諶、鄭玄舊圖，載其制度。

translations.literal: He himself says that in the third year of Xiande of Zhou, together with Tian Min and others, he followed the office of the jade-worker in the Offices of Zhou and the old diagrams of Ruan Chen and Zheng Xuan, recording their regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He says that in Later Zhou Xiande 3, working with Tian Min and others, he followed the jade-worker's duties in the Offices of Zhou and the old diagrams of Ruan Chen and Zheng Xuan to set down the specifications.

sentences.zh: 臣等按：《周禮》玉人之職，隻有「璧琮九寸」、「彖琮八寸」及「璧羨度尺、好三寸以為度」之文，即無蒼璧、黃琮之制。

translations.literal: We consider: in the office of the jade-worker in the Rites of Zhou there are only the passages "bi and cong nine inches," "large cong eight inches," and "the bi's surplus measure is one foot, the perforation three inches as the standard"—there are no regulations for an azure bi or yellow cong.
translations.idiomatic: We find that the jade-worker's chapter in the Rites of Zhou mentions only "bi and cong nine inches," "large cong eight inches," and "the bi's surplus measure is one foot, with a three-inch perforation as the standard"—nowhere does it prescribe an azure bi or yellow cong.

sentences.zh: 兼引注有《爾雅》「肉倍好」之說，此即是注「璧羨度」之文，又非蒼璧之制。

translations.literal: He also cites a commentary citing the Erya's saying that "the flesh is twice the perforation"; this is commentary on the passage about the bi's surplus measure, and again is not a regulation for the azure bi.
translations.idiomatic: He also cites commentary invoking the Erya's phrase that "the rim is twice the hole"—but that glosses the passage on the bi's surplus measure, not the azure bi.

sentences.zh: 又詳鄭玄自注《周禮》，不載尺寸，豈復別作畫圖，違經立異？

translations.literal: Moreover, examining Zheng Xuan's own commentary on the Rites of Zhou, it does not record dimensions—how could he separately have made painted diagrams that depart from the classics and establish divergent views?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Zheng Xuan's own commentary on the Rites of Zhou records no dimensions—how could he have produced separate illustrated diagrams that contradict the classics?

sentences.zh: 《四部書目》內有《三禮圖》十二卷，是隋開皇中敕禮官修撰。

translations.literal: Within the Bibliography of the Four Categories there is the Illustrations of the Three Rites in twelve scrolls, compiled on imperial order by ritual officials in the Kaihuang period of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The Bibliography of the Four Categories lists the Illustrations of the Three Rites in twelve scrolls, compiled on imperial order by ritual officials in Sui Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 其圖第一、第二題云「梁氏」，第十後題云「鄭氏」，又稱不知梁氏、鄭氏名位所出。

translations.literal: The first and second illustrations are titled "Mr. Liang"; from the tenth onward they are titled "Mr. Zheng"; it also states that the names and positions of Mr. Liang and Mr. Zheng are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The first and second diagrams are attributed to "Mr. Liang"; from the tenth onward to "Mr. Zheng"; the catalogue also notes that the identity and rank of these two men are unknown.

sentences.zh: 今書府有《三禮圖》，亦題「梁氏」、「鄭氏」，不言名位。

translations.literal: The present imperial library has the Illustrations of the Three Rites, likewise titled "Mr. Liang" and "Mr. Zheng," without stating names and positions.
translations.idiomatic: The palace library's copy of the Illustrations of the Three Rites likewise bears the labels "Mr. Liang" and "Mr. Zheng" without giving their full names or offices.

sentences.zh: 厥後有梁正者，集前代圖記更加詳議，題《三禮圖》曰：「陳留阮士信受《禮》學於潁川綦冊君，取其說，為圖三卷，多不按《禮》文而引漢事，與鄭君之文違錯。

translations.literal: Afterward there was Liang Zheng, who gathered diagrams and records of former ages and deliberated on them in greater detail; his Illustrations of the Three Rites states: "Ruan Shixin of Chenliu received ritual learning from Lord Ce of the Ce clan in Yingchuan; taking his doctrines, he made illustrations in three scrolls, mostly not following the ritual texts but citing Han affairs, in conflict and error with Master Zheng's writings.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang Zheng collected earlier diagrams and records and discussed them at greater length; his Illustrations of the Three Rites states: "Ruan Shixin of Chenliu studied ritual under Lord Ce of Yingchuan; adopting his views, he produced three scrolls of illustrations, often departing from the ritual texts to cite Han-dynasty practice, in conflict with Master Zheng's writings.

sentences.zh: 」正刪為二卷，其阮士信即諶也。

translations.literal: " Zheng reduced them to two scrolls; this Ruan Shixin is [Ruan] Chen.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng abridged the work to two scrolls; this Ruan Shixin is Ruan Chen.

sentences.zh: 如梁正之言，可知諶之紕謬。

translations.literal: As Liang Zheng's words show, one can know Chen's errors.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zheng's account alone shows how unreliable Ruan Chen was.

sentences.zh: 兼三卷《禮圖》刪為二卷，應在今《禮圖》之內，亦無改祭玉之說。

translations.literal: Moreover, the three-scroll Ritual Illustrations reduced to two scrolls should be within the present Ritual Illustrations, and likewise contain no proposal to alter sacrificial jades.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the three-scroll ritual diagrams abridged to two should be part of the present work, and they too contain no proposal to change the sacrificial jades.

sentences.zh: 臣等參詳自周公制禮之後，叔孫通重定以來，禮有緯書，漢代諸儒頗多著述，討尋祭玉，並無尺寸之說。

translations.literal: We have examined in detail that from after the Duke of Zhou established ritual, and since Shusun Tong's re-establishment, there are weft texts on ritual and Han scholars wrote extensively; in searching for [statements on] sacrificial jades, none give specifications of size.
translations.idiomatic: We have reviewed the record from the Duke of Zhou's establishment of ritual through Shusun Tong's restoration: although ritual weft texts exist and Han scholars wrote extensively, nowhere do we find dimensions specified for sacrificial jades.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉之後，鄭玄、王肅之學各有生徒，《三禮》、《六經》無不論說，檢其書，亦不言祭玉尺寸。

translations.literal: After Wei and Jin, the learning of Zheng Xuan and Wang Su each had disciples; the Three Rites and Six Classics were all discussed and explained—examining their books, they likewise do not speak of the dimensions of sacrificial jades.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei and Jin, the schools of Zheng Xuan and Wang Su each had disciples who commented on the Three Rites and Six Classics—yet examining their works, none specifies the dimensions of sacrificial jades.

sentences.zh: 臣等參驗畫圖本書，周公所說正經不言尺寸，設使後人謬為之說，安得便入周圖？

translations.literal: We have examined and verified the illustrated books: the orthodox classics spoken by the Duke of Zhou do not mention dimensions; even if later men erroneously made such statements, how could they simply be admitted into Zhou diagrams?
translations.idiomatic: We have checked the illustrated books against the canon: the orthodox classics attributed to the Duke of Zhou specify no dimensions; even if later writers invented such claims, how could they be admitted into Zhou ritual diagrams?

sentences.zh: 知崇義等以諸侯入朝獻天子夫人之琮璧以為祭玉，又配合「羨度」、「肉好」之言，強為尺寸，古今大禮，順非改非，於理未通。

translations.literal: Thus we know that Chongyi and others took the cong and bi presented by feudal lords when entering court to the Son of Heaven and his consort as sacrificial jades, and forcibly matched them with passages on "surplus measure" and "flesh and perforation" to impose dimensions—a great ritual of past and present, approving what is wrong and altering what is not wrong; in principle this cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly Chongyi and his allies took the cong and bi that feudal lords presented at court to the Son of Heaven and his consort and treated them as sacrificial jades, then forced dimensions by twisting passages on "surplus measure" and "rim and hole"—a distortion of a great rite observed through the ages that cannot stand to reason.

sentences.zh: 又據尹拙所述禮神之六玉，稱取梁桂州刺史崔靈恩所撰《三禮義宗》內「昊天及五精帝圭、璧、琮、璜皆長尺二寸，以法十二時；

translations.literal: Moreover, according to what Yin Zhuo stated about the six jades for sacrificing to the spirits, he said he took from the Comprehensive Meaning of the Three Rites by Cui Ling'en, Governor of Guizhou in Liang, the passage: "For August Heaven and the Five Essences the gui, bi, cong, and huang are each one foot two inches long, in accord with the twelve hours;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhuo also cited the six jades for spirit sacrifice, drawing on Cui Ling'en's Comprehensive Meaning of the Three Rites from Liang: "For August Heaven and the Five Essences the gui, bi, cong, and huang are each one foot two inches long, following the twelve hours;

sentences.zh: 祭地之琮長十寸，以效地之數。

translations.literal: the cong for sacrificing to Earth is ten inches long, in emulation of Earth's number."
translations.idiomatic: the cong for Earth sacrifice is ten inches long, matching Earth's number."

sentences.zh: 」又引《白虎通》云：「 方中圓外曰璧，圓中方外曰琮。

translations.literal: " He also cited the Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Hall: "Square within and round without is called bi; round within and square without is called cong.
translations.idiomatic: " He also quoted the Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Hall: "Square within and round without is called a bi; round within and square without is called a cong.

sentences.zh: 」崇義非之，以為靈恩非周公之才，無周公之位，一朝撰述，便補六玉闕文，尤不合禮。

translations.literal: " Chongyi rejected this, holding that Ling'en was not the Duke of Zhou's talent and had not the Duke of Zhou's position; in a single morning's composition he patched the missing text on the six jades—especially contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongyi objected, arguing that Ling'en was neither the Duke of Zhou's equal in talent nor in rank, and that to compose a work in a single effort and supply missing text on the six jades was especially unorthodox.

sentences.zh: 臣等竊以劉向之論《洪範》，王通之作《元經》，非必挺聖人之姿，而居上公之位，有益於教，不為斐然。

translations.literal: We privately consider that Liu Xiang's discussion of the Great Plan and Wang Tong's composition of the Original Classic did not necessarily require possessing a sage's stature and holding a highest-duke's position; if they benefit instruction, they are not mere ornament.
translations.idiomatic: We would note that Liu Xiang's commentary on the Great Plan and Wang Tong's Original Classic were not written by men who possessed a sage's stature or held a highest duke's rank—yet because they served instruction, they were not mere flourish.

sentences.zh: 臣等以靈恩所撰之書，聿稽古訓，祭玉以十二為數者，蓋天有十二次，地有十二辰，日有十二時，封山之玉牒十二寸，圜丘之籩豆十二列，天子以鎮圭外守，宗後以大琮內守，皆長尺有二寸。

translations.literal: We hold that Ling'en's book traces ancient teaching: sacrificial jades taking twelve as their number—Heaven has twelve stations, Earth has twelve branches, the day has twelve hours; the jade document for the Feng sacrifice is twelve inches, the stands and dishes at the Round Mound are twelve rows; the Son of Heaven with the tablet gui guards outward, the queen with the great cong guards inward—all are one foot two inches long.
translations.idiomatic: Ling'en's work follows ancient teaching: sacrificial jades take twelve as their number because Heaven has twelve stations, Earth twelve branches, and the day twelve hours; the jade document for the Feng sacrifice is twelve inches, the stands at the Round Mound altar twelve rows; the Son of Heaven's tablet gui and the queen's great cong—all are one foot two inches long.

sentences.zh: 又祼圭尺二寸，王者以祀宗廟。

translations.literal: Moreover, the libation gui is one foot two inches; the king uses it to sacrifice at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The libation gui is likewise one foot two inches, which the king uses in ancestral temple sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 若人君親行之郊祭，登壇酌獻，服大裘，搢大圭，行稽奠，而手秉尺二之圭，神獻九寸之璧，不及禮宗廟祼圭之數，父天母地，情亦奚安？

translations.literal: If the ruler in person performs the suburban sacrifice, ascends the altar, pours and presents offerings, wears the great fur robe, inserts the great gui, performs the bowing presentation, yet in hand holds a gui of one foot two inches while presenting to the spirits a bi of nine inches—not reaching the measure of the ancestral temple's libation gui—how can the sentiment toward Heaven as father and Earth as mother be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler personally conducts the suburban sacrifice, ascends the altar in his great fur robe with the great gui inserted, performs the bowing presentation, yet holds a one-foot-two gui while offering the spirits a nine-inch bi—less than the ancestral temple's libation gui—how can he honor Heaven as father and Earth as mother with a clear conscience?

sentences.zh: 則靈恩議論，理未為失，所以自《義宗》之出，曆梁、陳、隋、唐垂四百年，言禮者引為師法，今《五禮精義》、《開元禮》、《郊祀錄》皆引《義宗》為標準。

translations.literal: Then Ling'en's arguments are not wrong in principle; therefore from the appearance of the Comprehensive Meaning through Liang, Chen, Sui, and Tang for nearly four hundred years, those who spoke of ritual cited it as authoritative method; now the Essentials of the Five Rites, the Kaiyuan Rites, and the Record of Suburban Sacrifice all cite the Comprehensive Meaning as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Ling'en's reasoning is not unsound; from the Comprehensive Meaning's appearance through Liang, Chen, Sui, and Tang—nearly four hundred years—ritualists have cited it as authoritative, and the Essentials of the Five Rites, Kaiyuan Rites, and Record of Suburban Sacrifice all take it as their standard.

sentences.zh: 近代晉、漢兩朝，仍依舊制。

translations.literal: In recent times the two dynasties of Jin [Later Jin] and Han [Later Han] still followed the old system.
translations.idiomatic: The recent Later Jin and Later Han dynasties likewise followed the established practice.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，田敏等妄作穿鑿，輒有更改。

translations.literal: In the Xiande period of Zhou, Tian Min and others recklessly made forced interpretations and rashly made changes.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Zhou Xiande, Tian Min and others forced strained interpretations and made arbitrary changes.

sentences.zh: 自唐貞觀之後，凡三次大修五禮，並因隋朝典故，或節奏繁簡之間稍有厘革，亦無改祭玉之說。

translations.literal: From after Tang Zhenguan there were three great revisions of the Five Rites in all, all following Sui precedents; even where between complexity and simplicity there were slight adjustments, there was likewise no proposal to alter sacrificial jades.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang Zhenguan there have been three major revisions of the Five Rites, all drawing on Sui precedent; even where complexity was adjusted, none proposed changing the sacrificial jades.

sentences.zh: 伏望依《白虎通》、《義宗》、唐禮之制，以為定式。

translations.literal: We humbly hope to follow the systems of the Comprehensive Discussions, the Comprehensive Meaning, and Tang ritual as the fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully ask that the standards of the Comprehensive Discussions, the Comprehensive Meaning, and Tang ritual be adopted as the fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 又尹拙依舊圖畫釜，聶崇義去釜畫鑊。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yin Zhuo followed the old illustrations in drawing the cauldron (fu), while Nie Chongyi removed the cauldron and drew the cooking pot (huo).
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhuo followed the old diagrams in depicting the fu cauldron, while Nie Chongyi removed the fu and depicted the huo pot instead.

sentences.zh: 臣等參詳舊圖，皆有釜無鑊。

translations.literal: We have examined the old illustrations in detail: all have the fu and none have the huo.
translations.idiomatic: We have reviewed the old diagrams: all show the fu cauldron and none the huo pot.

sentences.zh: 按《易·說卦》云「坤為釜」，《詩》云「惟錡及釜」，又云「溉之釜鬵」，《春秋傳》云「錡釜之器」，《禮記》云「燔黍捭豚」，解云「古未有甑釜，所以燔捭而祭。

translations.literal: According to the Explanation of the Trigrams in the Changes: "Kun is the cauldron"; the Odes say "only the cauldron and fu," and again "pour into the fu and xin"; the Spring and Autumn Commentary says "implements of cauldron and fu"; the Record of Rites says "roast millet and split the piglet," with commentary: "In antiquity there was not yet the steamer or fu, and therefore they roasted and split for sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The Explanation of the Trigrams in the Changes says "Kun represents the cauldron"; the Odes mention "only the cauldron and fu," and "pour into the fu and xin"; the Zuo Commentary speaks of "cauldron and fu vessels"; the Record of Rites describes "roasting millet and splitting the piglet," glossed as: "In antiquity there were no steamers or fu cauldrons, so food was roasted and split for sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 」即釜之為用，其來尚矣，故入於《禮圖》。

translations.literal: " Thus the use of the fu is of long standing, and therefore it entered the Ritual Illustrations.
translations.idiomatic: " The fu cauldron has been in use since antiquity, which is why it belongs in the ritual diagrams.

sentences.zh: 今崇義以《周官》祭祀有省鼎鑊，供鼎鑊，又以《儀禮》有羊鑊、豕鑊之文，乃雲畫釜不如畫鑊。

translations.literal: Now Chongyi, because the Offices of Zhou on sacrifice has "inspect the tripods and huo" and "supply the tripods and huo," and because the Ceremonies has passages on the sheep huo and pig huo, therefore says that drawing the fu is inferior to drawing the huo.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi, citing the Offices of Zhou's passages on inspecting and supplying tripods and huo pots, and the Ceremonies' references to sheep and pig huo pots, argues that depicting the fu is less appropriate than depicting the huo.

sentences.zh: 今諸經皆載釜之用，誠不可去。

translations.literal: Now all the classics record the use of the fu; it truly cannot be removed.
translations.idiomatic: All the classics record the use of the fu cauldron; it truly cannot be omitted.

sentences.zh: 又《周》、《儀禮》皆有鑊之文，請兩圖之。

translations.literal: Moreover, both the Offices of Zhou and the Ceremonies have passages on the huo; we ask that both be illustrated.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, both the Offices of Zhou and the Ceremonies mention the huo pot; we ask that both vessels be illustrated.

sentences.zh: 又若觀諸家祭祀之畫，今代見行之禮，於大祀前一日，光祿卿省視鼎鑊。

translations.literal: Moreover, if one observes the sacrificial paintings of various schools and the rites currently practiced in our age, on the day before a great sacrifice the Director of the Imperial Commissary inspects the tripods and huo.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, examining various schools' sacrificial illustrations and the rites practiced today, on the day before a great sacrifice the Director of the Imperial Commissary inspects the tripods and huo pots.

sentences.zh: 伏請圖鑊於鼎下。

translations.literal: We humbly request that the huo be illustrated beneath the tripod.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully ask that the huo pot be illustrated beneath the tripod.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed [their view].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved their recommendation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，崇義卒，《三禮圖》遂行於世，並畫於國子監講堂之壁。

translations.literal: Before long Chongyi died; the Illustrations of the Three Rites thereupon circulated in the world and were also painted on the walls of the lecture hall at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chongyi died; the Illustrations of the Three Rites thereafter circulated widely and were painted on the walls of the imperial university lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 崇義為學官，兼掌禮，僅二十年，世推其該博。

translations.literal: Chongyi served as a university official and concurrently managed ritual for nearly twenty years; the age praised his comprehensive learning.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi served as a university official and concurrently oversaw ritual affairs for nearly twenty years; his contemporaries esteemed his encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 郭忠恕嘗以其姓嘲之曰：「近貴全為聵，攀龍即作聾。

translations.literal: Guo Zhongshu once mocked him on account of his surname, saying: "Drawing near the noble, one becomes entirely deaf; climbing the dragon, one becomes hard of hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhongshu once mocked him through a pun on his surname: "Drawing near the noble, one turns wholly deaf; climbing the dragon, one becomes hard of hearing.

sentences.zh: 雖然三個耳，其奈不成聰。

translations.literal: Although there are three 'ears' [in the character 聶], how can one become truly acute of hearing?"
translations.idiomatic: Though you have three 'ears' in your name, you still cannot hear clearly."

sentences.zh: 」崇義對曰：「仆不能為詩，聊以一聯奉答。

translations.literal: " Chongyi replied: "Your servant cannot compose poetry; I offer but a single couplet in reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongyi replied: "I am no poet, but let me answer with a single couplet.

sentences.zh: 」即云：「勿笑有三耳，全勝畜二心。

translations.literal: " He then said: "Do not laugh at three ears—altogether superior to harboring two hearts."
translations.idiomatic: " He said: "Do not mock my three ears—they are far better than harboring two hearts."

sentences.zh: 」蓋因其名以嘲之。

translations.literal: " This was because he mocked him through his name.
translations.idiomatic: " He had turned the jest back on Zhongshu through his name.

sentences.zh: 忠恕大慚，人許其機捷而不失正，真儒者之戲雲。

translations.literal: Zhongshu was greatly ashamed; people approved his quick wit without losing propriety—truly a Confucian's jest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu was deeply embarrassed; people praised Chongyi's quick wit without loss of decorum—a true scholar's repartee.

sentences.zh: 邢昺，字叔明，曹州濟陰人。

translations.literal: Xing Bing, courtesy name Shuming, was a man of Jiyin in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Bing, courtesy name Shuming, was from Jiyin in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初舉《五經》，廷試日，召升殿講《師》、《比》二卦，又問以群經發題。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was selected in the Five Classics; on the day of the palace examination he was summoned to ascend the hall and lecture on the hexagrams Shi and Bi, and was further questioned with topics drawn from the various classics.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taiping Xingguo he qualified in the Five Classics examination; on the day of the palace test he was summoned to the hall to lecture on the Shi and Bi hexagrams and was further questioned on topics drawn from the classics.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉其精博，擢《九經》及第，授大理評事、知泰州鹽城監，賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: Taizong praised his thorough mastery and advanced him to pass the Nine Classics with highest honors, appointing him Evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of the Yancheng Salt Office in Taizhou, bestowing two hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong commended his mastery and passed him at the top of the Nine Classics examination, appointing him evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review and superintendent of the Yancheng salt office in Taizhou, with a grant of two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 昺以是監處楚、泰間，泰僻左而楚會要，鹽食為急，請改隸楚州，從之。

translations.literal: Bing, because this office lay between Chu and Tai, [found that] Tai was remote on the left while Chu was a key junction; salt and food were urgent needs, and he requested that it be transferred to subordination under Chuzhou—the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Because this salt office lay between Chu and Tai prefectures—Tai being remote while Chu was a major junction where salt and grain were urgently needed—Bing requested that it be placed under Chuzhou, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年，召為國子監丞，專講學之任。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as Assistant Director of the Imperial University with exclusive duty for lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to serve as assistant director of the imperial university, charged solely with lecturing.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書博士，出知儀州，就轉國子博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Doctor of the Secretariat, went out to serve as prefect of Yizhou, and was thereupon transferred to Doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretariat doctor, sent out as prefect of Yizhou, and then transferred to university doctor.

sentences.zh: 代還，賜緋，選為諸王府侍講。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he was granted scarlet robes and selected as lecturer for the various princely establishments.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to court, he received scarlet robes and was appointed lecturer to the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，遷水部員外郎，改司勳。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi period he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Waterways and changed to the Ministry of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Waterways and then transferred to the Ministry of Merit.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，賜金紫，累遷金部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duan Gong he was granted gold and purple, and was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Duan Gong he received gold and purple insignia and was promoted repeatedly until he became director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，上言：「亡兄素嘗舉進士，願沾贈典。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde he submitted a memorial: "My deceased elder brother once took the jinshi examination; I wish that he may share in a posthumous bestowal."
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 2 he memorialized: "My late elder brother once sat for the jinshi examination; I ask that he receive a posthumous honor."

sentences.zh: 」特贈大理評事。

translations.literal: " He was specially posthumously granted Evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: " The court specially posthumously granted him the rank of evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 是夏，上幸國子監閱庫書，問昺經版幾何，昺曰：「國初不及四千，今十餘萬，經、傳、正義皆具。

translations.literal: That summer the emperor visited the Imperial University to inspect the library collections and asked Bing how many classic blocks there were; Bing said: "At the founding of the state there were fewer than four thousand; now there are more than a hundred thousand, with classics, commentaries, and authoritative exegeses all complete.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the emperor visited the imperial university to inspect the library and asked how many classic printing blocks there were; Bing replied: "At the founding there were fewer than four thousand; now there are more than a hundred thousand, with classics, commentaries, and authoritative exegeses all in place.

sentences.zh: 臣少從師業儒時，經具有疏者百無一二，蓋力不能傳寫。

translations.literal: When your subject in youth followed teachers in Confucian studies, of classics with commentaries there were scarcely one or two in a hundred, for the most part because one lacked the means to copy and transmit them.
translations.idiomatic: When I was young and studying under my teachers, scarcely one classic in a hundred had a commentary available—we simply could not afford to copy them.

sentences.zh: 今板本大備，士庶家皆有之，斯乃儒者逢辰之幸也。

translations.literal: Now printed editions are greatly complete and scholar and commoner households all have them—this is the good fortune of Confucians encountering their time.
translations.idiomatic: Now printed editions are abundantly available in every scholar's and commoner's home—this is the great fortune of Confucians living in a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 」上喜曰：「國家雖尚儒術，非四方無事，何以及此！

translations.literal: " The emperor said with pleasure: "Although the state esteems Confucian learning, had not the four quarters been free of trouble, how could we have reached this!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said with pleasure: "Though our state honors Confucian learning, had the realm not been at peace, how could we have achieved this!"

sentences.zh: 」上又訪以學館故事，有未振舉者，昺不能有所建明。

translations.literal: " The emperor also inquired about precedents of the academic halls, asking whether anything had not been revived; Bing was unable to offer any constructive proposals.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also asked about academic-hall precedents that had fallen into disuse; Bing could offer no constructive proposals.

sentences.zh: 先是，印書所裁餘紙，鬻以供監中雜用，昺請歸之三司，以裨國用。

translations.literal: Previously, trimmings from the printing office were sold to supply miscellaneous expenses at the Directorate; Bing requested that they be returned to the Three Departments to supplement state revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the printing office had sold its paper trimmings to cover miscellaneous university expenses; Bing asked that these proceeds be turned over to the fiscal authorities to supplement state revenue.

sentences.zh: 自是監學公費不給，講官亦厭其寥落。

translations.literal: From this time the public funds of the Directorate of Education were insufficient, and the lecturers also grew weary of its desolation.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the university's public funds fell short, and the lecturers too wearied of its sparse attendance.

sentences.zh: 上方興起道術，又令昺與張雍、杜鎬、孫奭舉經術該博、德行端良者，以廣學員。

translations.literal: The emperor was then promoting the Way and learning, and again ordered Bing together with Zhang Yong, Du Hao, and Sun Shi to recommend men comprehensive in classical learning and upright in conduct, in order to expand the student body.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then promoting scholarship and again ordered Bing, together with Zhang Yong, Du Hao, and Sun Shi, to recommend men of broad classical learning and upright conduct to enlarge the student body.

sentences.zh: 三年，加刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 昺居近職，常多召對，一日從容與上語及宮邸舊僚，歎其淪喪殆盡，唯昺獨存。

translations.literal: Bing held a post near the throne and was often summoned for audience; one day, at ease, he spoke with the emperor of old colleagues from the princely establishment, lamenting that they had nearly all perished and only Bing remained.
translations.idiomatic: Bing held a post close to the throne and was often summoned; one day, speaking at ease with the emperor of old colleagues from the princely household, he lamented that nearly all had died and he alone survived.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賜白金千兩，且詔其妻至宮庭，賜以冠帔。

translations.literal: The next day he was granted a thousand taels of white gold, and an edict summoned his wife to the palace, bestowing cap and robe.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he received a thousand taels of white gold, and the emperor summoned his wife to the palace and bestowed official cap and robe upon her.

sentences.zh: 四年，昺以羸老艱於趨步上前，自陳曹州故鄉，願給假一年歸視田里，俟明年郊祀還朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Bing, enfeebled by age and finding it hard to advance in steps, came forward and stated that his old home was in Caozhou and he wished a year's leave to visit his fields, returning to court after next year's suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Bing, frail with age and finding it difficult to walk, petitioned that his home was in Caozhou and asked for a year's leave to visit his fields, promising to return after the coming suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 上命坐，慰勞之，因謂曰：「便可權本州，何須假耶？

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to sit and comforted him, saying: "You may as well hold acting appointment in your home prefecture—why need leave?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bade him sit, comforted him, and said, "You may as well serve as acting prefect of your home district—why request leave?"

sentences.zh: 」昺又言楊礪、夏侯嶠同為府僚，二臣沒皆贈尚書。

translations.literal: Bing also said that Yang Li and Xiahou Qiao had been fellow officials in the princely establishment; when the two ministers died they were both posthumously granted the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Bing also noted that Yang Li and Xiahou Qiao had served with him in the princely household; when those two ministers died they were both posthumously made secretariat ministers.

sentences.zh: 上憫之，翌日，謂宰相曰：「此可見其志矣。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity; the next day he said to the chief ministers: "This shows his intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved; the next day he told the chief ministers, "This shows what he wants."

sentences.zh: 」即超拜工部尚書、知曹州、職如故。

translations.literal: He was thereupon promoted to Minister of Works, made prefect of Caozhou, with duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately promoted to Minister of Works and appointed prefect of Caozhou, retaining his other duties.

sentences.zh: 入辭日，賜襲衣、金帶。

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience he was granted court robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took leave he received court robes and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 是日，特開龍圖閣，召近臣宴崇和殿，上作五、七言詩二首賜之，預宴者皆賦。

translations.literal: That day the Dragon Diagram Hall was specially opened and nearby officials were summoned to a banquet at the Chonghe Hall; the emperor composed two poems in five- and seven-character lines to bestow on him, and all who attended the banquet composed verses.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Dragon Diagram Pavilion was opened specially and nearby officials were banqueted in the Chonghe Hall; the emperor composed two poems in five- and seven-syllable lines as gifts, and every guest present wrote verses in return.

sentences.zh: 昺視壁間《尚書》、《禮記圖》，指《中庸》篇曰：凡為天下國家有九經。

translations.literal: Bing looked at the Illustrations of the Documents and the Record of Rites on the wall and, pointing to the chapter on the Mean, said: "In governing the realm and the state there are nine principles."
translations.idiomatic: Bing looked at the wall illustrations of the Documents and the Record of Rites and, pointing to the chapter on the Mean, cited its line: "In governing the realm and the state there are nine principles."

sentences.zh: 因陳其大義，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: He thereupon set forth its great meaning, and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He then expounded its larger meaning, which the emperor praised and accepted.

sentences.zh: 及行，又令近臣祖送，設會於宜春苑。

translations.literal: When he departed, the emperor again ordered nearby officials to escort him on his way and held a feast at the Yichun Garden.
translations.idiomatic: As he set out, the emperor again had nearby officials see him off and held a farewell feast at the Yichun Garden.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，上東封泰山，昺表曹州民請車駕經由本州，仍令濟陰令王範部送父老詣闕，優詔答之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu the emperor was to perform the eastern Feng and Tai sacrifices; Bing memorialized that the people of Caozhou requested that the imperial carriage pass through their prefecture, and also had Jiyin magistrate Wang Fan escort elders to the capital; a gracious edict answered them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Dazhong Xiangfu, as the emperor prepared to worship Heaven and Earth at Mount Tai, Bing memorialized that the people of Caozhou asked that the imperial procession pass through their prefecture and had the Jiyin magistrate Wang Fan escort local elders to court; the emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 俄召還。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 車駕進發，命判留司御史臺。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession set out, he was ordered to preside over the Censorate left at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession departed, he was ordered to preside over the capital censorate in the emperor's absence.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，進位禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was advanced to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 上勤政憫農，每雨雪不時，憂形於色，以昺素習田事，多委曲訪之。

translations.literal: The emperor was diligent in government and compassionate toward farmers; whenever rain and snow came untimely he showed worry on his face, and because Bing was versed in farming affairs he often questioned him in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worked diligently and cared for farmers; whenever rain or snow came at the wrong season his worry showed on his face, and because Bing knew farming well the emperor often questioned him at length.

sentences.zh: 初，田家察陰晴豐凶，皆有狀候，老農之相傳者率有驗，昺多采其說為對。

translations.literal: Formerly, farming households observed omens of clear or cloudy weather, abundance or famine, all with signs; what old farmers transmitted was mostly verified, and Bing often adopted their sayings in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers had long observed signs of fair or foul weather and good or bad harvests, and the lore old peasants passed down was usually reliable; Bing often drew on their sayings in his answers.

sentences.zh: 又言：「民之災患，大者有四：一曰，疫，二曰旱，三曰水，四曰畜。

translations.literal: He also said: "Among the people's calamities, the great ones are four: first, pestilence; second, drought; third, flood; fourth, locusts."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The people's great calamities are four: pestilence, drought, flood, and locusts."

sentences.zh: 災歲必有其一，但或輕或重耳。

translations.literal: "In years of disaster there is always one of them, only sometimes light or heavy."
translations.idiomatic: "In disaster years at least one of these always appears, though sometimes lightly and sometimes severely."

sentences.zh: 四事之害，旱暵為甚，蓋田無畎澮，悉不可救，所損必盡。

translations.literal: "Of the harm of the four, drought is the worst, for when fields lack irrigation channels nothing can be saved and the loss is total."
translations.idiomatic: "Of the four, drought does the greatest harm, for when fields lack irrigation ditches nothing can be saved and the loss is complete."

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『天災流行，國家代有。

translations.literal: "The Commentary says: "When Heaven's calamities spread, each state has them in turn.""
translations.idiomatic: "The Commentary says, "When Heaven's calamities spread abroad, every state suffers them in turn.""

sentences.zh: 』此之謂也。」

translations.literal: "This is what is meant.""
translations.idiomatic: "That is what is meant.""

sentences.zh: 三年，被病請告，詔太醫診視。

translations.literal: In the third year he fell ill and requested sick leave; an edict ordered the imperial physicians to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he fell ill and asked for sick leave; the emperor ordered imperial physicians to attend him.

sentences.zh: 六月，上親臨問疾，賜名藥一奩、白金器千兩、繒彩千匹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the emperor personally visited to inquire after his illness and bestowed a box of famous medicines, a thousand taels of silver vessels, and a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor personally visited him in his illness and bestowed a casket of famous medicines, a thousand taels of silver vessels, and a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 國朝故事，非宗戚將相，無省疾臨喪之禮，特有加於昺與郭贄者，以恩舊故也。

translations.literal: By the court's precedent, except for imperial kin and chief ministers there was no ritual of visiting the sick or attending the mourning; the special favor shown Bing and Guo Zan was because of old ties.
translations.idiomatic: By court precedent only imperial kin and chief ministers received visits in illness or attendance at mourning; the special honor shown Bing and Guo Zan was due to long friendship with the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有旨命中書召其子太常博士知東明縣仲寶、國子博士知信陽軍若思還侍疾。

translations.literal: Before long an order directed the Secretariat to summon his son, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Doctor and magistrate of Dongming County Zhongbao, and his son, Imperial University Doctor and military prefect of Xinyang Ruosi, to return and attend his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an order directed the Secretariat to recall his sons—Zhongbao, doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and magistrate of Dongming County, and Ruosi, university doctor and military prefect of Xinyang—to attend him in his illness.

sentences.zh: 逾月卒，年七十九，贈左僕射，三子並進秩。

translations.literal: After more than a month he died, aged seventy-nine; he was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and all three sons were advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he died at seventy-nine; he was posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and all three sons were promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 初，雍熙中，昺撰《禮選》二十卷獻之，太宗探其帙，得《文王世子篇》，觀之甚悅，因問衛紹欽曰：「昺為諸王講說，曾及此乎？

translations.literal: Formerly, in the Yongxi period Bing compiled Selected Rites in twenty scrolls and presented them; Taizong opened the bundle and found the chapter on the Heir of King Wen; viewing it he was greatly pleased and asked Wei Shaoqin: "When Bing lectured for the princes, did he ever reach this?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Yongxi, Bing compiled Selected Rites in twenty scrolls and presented them; Taizong opened the bundle, found the chapter on the heir of King Wen, and was greatly pleased, asking Wei Shaoqin, "When Bing lectured to the princes, did he ever reach this passage?"

sentences.zh: 」紹欽曰：「諸王常時訪昺經義，昺每至發明君臣父子之道，必重復陳之。

translations.literal: Shaoqin said: "The princes often inquired of Bing on the meaning of the classics; whenever Bing reached the Way of ruler and minister, father and son, he always repeated it."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqin replied, "The princes often asked Bing about the classics; whenever he expounded the relations of ruler and minister, father and son, he always stressed them repeatedly."

sentences.zh: 」太宗益喜。

translations.literal: Taizong was still more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was still more pleased.

sentences.zh: 上嘗因內閣暴書，覽而稱善，召昺同觀，作《禮選讚》賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor once, because books were aired in the inner library, looked through them and praised them, summoned Bing to view them together, and composed an encomium on Selected Rites to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while books were being aired in the inner library, the emperor looked through them, praised them, summoned Bing to view them with him, and composed an encomium on Selected Rites as a gift.

sentences.zh: 昺言：「家無遺稿，願得副本。

translations.literal: Bing said: "My household has no surviving draft; I wish to obtain a copy."
translations.idiomatic: Bing said, "No draft survives in my home; I would like a copy."

sentences.zh: 」上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 繕錄未畢而昺卒，亟詔寫二本，一本賜其家，一本俾置塚中。

translations.literal: The copying was not finished when Bing died; the emperor urgently ordered two copies written, one bestowed on his family and one placed in his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Copying was not finished when Bing died; the emperor urgently ordered two copies made, one for his family and one placed in his tomb.

sentences.zh: 昺在東宮及內庭，侍上講《孝經》、《禮記》、《論語》、《書》、《易》、《詩》、《左氏傳》。

translations.literal: Bing in the Eastern Palace and within the inner court attended the emperor in lecturing on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Record of Rites, the Analects, the Documents, the Changes, the Odes, and the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Palace and within the inner court Bing lectured the emperor on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Record of Rites, the Analects, the Documents, the Changes, the Odes, and the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 據傳疏敷引之外，多引時事為喻，深被嘉獎。

translations.literal: Beyond citing the commentaries he often drew on current affairs as illustrations and was deeply praised and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond citing the commentaries he often illustrated points with current affairs and won deep praise and reward.

sentences.zh: 上嘗問：「管仲、召忽皆事公子糾，小白之入，召忽死之，管仲乃歸齊相桓公。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked: "Guan Zhong and Zhao Hu both served Prince Jiu; when Xiao Bai entered [Qi], Zhao Hu died for him while Guan Zhong returned to Qi and became chief minister to Duke Huan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked, "Guan Zhong and Zhao Hu both served Prince Jiu; when Duke Huan entered Qi, Zhao Hu died for his lord while Guan Zhong returned and became Duke Huan's chief minister."

sentences.zh: 豈非召忽以忠死，而管仲不能固其節，為臣之道當若是乎？

translations.literal: "Was it not that Zhao Hu died in loyalty while Guan Zhong could not hold fast to his integrity—is this how a minister should act?"
translations.idiomatic: "Was Zhao Hu loyal unto death while Guan Zhong failed to hold to his integrity—is that how a minister should behave?"

sentences.zh: 又鄭注《禮記·世子篇》云：『文王以勤憂損壽，武王以安樂延年。

translations.literal: "Moreover, Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Record of Rites chapter on the heir says: "King Wen shortened his life through anxious toil, while King Wu prolonged his life through ease and joy.""
translations.idiomatic: "And Zheng Xuan's commentary on the chapter on the heir in the Record of Rites says, "King Wen shortened his life through anxious toil, while King Wu prolonged his through ease and joy.""

sentences.zh: 』朕以為本經旨意必不然也。

translations.literal: "I consider that the original meaning of the classic cannot be so."
translations.idiomatic: "I do not believe the original meaning of the classic can be so."

sentences.zh: 且夏禹焦勞，有玄圭之賜，而享國永年。

translations.literal: "Moreover, Yu of Xia toiled anxiously and received the dark jade tablet, yet enjoyed the state for many years."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, Yu of Xia labored exhaustingly, received the dark jade tablet, and yet enjoyed a long reign."

sentences.zh: 若文王能憂人之心，不自暇逸，縱無感應，豈至虧損壽命耶？

translations.literal: "If King Wen could care for others' hearts and never rest himself, even without a divine response, how could his life have been shortened?"
translations.idiomatic: "If King Wen truly cared for others and never rested, even without a miraculous sign, how could his life have been shortened?"

sentences.zh: 」各隨其事理以對。

translations.literal: "Each answered according to the principle of the matter."
translations.idiomatic: "Bing answered each question according to its principle."

sentences.zh: 先是，咸平中，王欽若知貢舉，有告其受舉人賄賂者，下御史臺鞫得狀，欽若自訴，詔昺與邊肅、毋賓古、閻承翰就太常寺覆推。

translations.literal: Previously, in the Xianping period Wang Qinruo directed the examinations; someone reported that he had accepted bribes from candidates; the matter was sent to the Censorate and the facts were established; Qinruo appealed, and an edict ordered Bing, Bian Su, Wu Binggu, and Yan Chenghan to go to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for a rehearing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Xianping, Wang Qinruo directed the civil examinations; someone reported that he had accepted bribes from candidates; the censorate established the facts; Qinruo appealed; and an edict ordered Bing, Bian Su, Wu Binggu, and Yan Chenghan to rehear the case at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 昺力辨欽若，而洪湛抵罪，欽若以是德之。

translations.literal: Bing forcefully argued for Qinruo, while Hong Zhan was convicted; Qinruo therefore owed him a debt of gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Bing vigorously defended Qinruo while Hong Zhan was convicted; Qinruo therefore felt indebted to him.

sentences.zh: 昺之厚被寵顧，欽若與有功焉。

translations.literal: That Bing was greatly favored owed something to Qinruo's contribution.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's great favor at court owed something to Qinruo's help.

sentences.zh: 仲寶貪猥不才，舉止率易，士大夫多鄙笑之。

translations.literal: Zhongbao was greedy, base, and without talent; his conduct was careless and easy, and most scholar-officials despised and laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongbao was greedy, incompetent, and coarse in manner; most scholar-officials despised and ridiculed him.

sentences.zh: 欽若在中書，用為三司判官，後至祠部郎中，坐贓黜官，卒。

translations.literal: When Qinruo was in the Secretariat he employed him as an auditor of the Three Departments; later he reached Director in the Ministry of Rites, was dismissed for corruption, and died.
translations.idiomatic: While Qinruo served in the Secretariat he appointed Zhongbao an auditor of the Three Departments; later he rose to director in the Ministry of Rites, was dismissed for corruption, and died.

sentences.zh: 若思終於駕部郎中。

translations.literal: Ruosi ended his career as Director in the Ministry of Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Ruosi ended his career as director in the Ministry of Transport.

sentences.zh: 孫奭，字宗古，博州博平人。

translations.literal: Sun Shi, courtesy name Zonggu, was a man of Boping in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shi, courtesy name Zonggu, was from Boping in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 幼與諸生師里中王徹，徹死，有從奭問經者，奭為解析微指，人人驚服，於是門人數百皆從奭。

translations.literal: In youth he studied with the village teacher Wang Che; after Che died, when there were those who came to Shi to inquire about the classics, Shi would parse the subtle points, and everyone was amazed and submitted—thereupon several hundred disciples all followed Shi.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under the village teacher Wang Che; after Che died, those who came to Shi with questions on the classics found him able to explain subtle points so clearly that everyone was astonished, and several hundred disciples followed him.

sentences.zh: 後徙居須城。

translations.literal: Later he moved to Xucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he moved to Xucheng.

sentences.zh: 《九經》及第，為莒縣主簿，上書願試講說，遷大理評事，為國子監直講。

translations.literal: He passed the Nine Classics with highest honors, served as recorder of Juxian County, memorialized requesting a trial lecture, was promoted to Evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review, and became Lecturer at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Nine Classics examination with highest honors, served as recorder of Juxian County, petitioned for a trial lecture, was promoted to evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review, and became lecturer at the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸國子監，召奭講《書》，至「事不師古，以克永世，匪說攸聞」，帝曰：「此至言也。

translations.literal: Taizong visited the Imperial University, summoned Shi to lecture on the Documents, and when he reached "If affairs do not follow antiquity, they will not long endure—this is not what I have heard from you," the emperor said: "These are utmost words."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong visited the imperial university and summoned Shi to lecture on the Documents; when he reached the line "If affairs do not follow antiquity they will not long endure—this is not what I have heard from you," the emperor said, "These are words of the highest wisdom."

sentences.zh: 商宗乃得賢相如此耶！

translations.literal: "Did the Shang sovereign obtain such an worthy minister as this!"
translations.idiomatic: "Did the Shang ruler truly obtain such a worthy minister as this!"

sentences.zh: 」因谘嗟久之。

translations.literal: He sighed and lamented for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 賜五品服。

translations.literal: He was granted fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted robes of the fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 真宗以為諸王府侍讀。

translations.literal: Zhenzong made him lecturer to the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong appointed him lecturer to the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 會詔百官轉對，奭上十事。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered all officials to present rotating memorials, Shi submitted ten items.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered all officials to submit rotating memorials, Shi presented ten proposals.

sentences.zh: 判太常禮院、國子監、司農寺，累遷工部郎中，擢龍圖閣待制。

translations.literal: He served as judge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Imperial University, and the Ministry of Agriculture, was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works, and was elevated to Attendant Gentleman of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the imperial university, and the Ministry of Agriculture, rose to director in the Ministry of Works, and was elevated to attendant gentleman of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 奭以經術進，守道自處，即有所言，未嘗阿附取悅。

translations.literal: Shi advanced through classical learning and maintained himself by holding to the Way; in whatever he spoke he never flattered to please.
translations.idiomatic: Shi rose through classical learning and held to the Way; in whatever he said he never flattered to please.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，得天書於左承天門，帝將奉迎，召宰相對崇政殿西廡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu the Heavenly Writ was obtained at the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven; the emperor was about to go forth to receive it and summoned the chief ministers to the western gallery of the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Dazhong Xiangfu the Heavenly Writ appeared at the Left Gate of Accepting Heaven; as the emperor prepared to receive it he summoned the chief ministers to the western gallery of the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 王旦等曰：「天貺符命，實盛德之應。

translations.literal: Wang Dan and others said: "Heaven's bestowal of the talisman mandate is truly the response of supreme virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan and others said, "Heaven's gift of the talisman mandate is truly the response of supreme virtue."

sentences.zh: 」皆再拜稱萬歲。

translations.literal: All bowed twice and shouted "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: All bowed twice and shouted long life to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 又召問奭，奭對曰：「臣愚，所聞『天何言哉』，豈有書也？

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned Shi and asked him; Shi replied: "Your subject is foolish; what I have heard is "Does Heaven speak?"—how could there be a book?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Shi again; Shi replied, "I am foolish; what I have heard is that Heaven does not speak—how could there be a book?"

sentences.zh: 」帝既奉迎天書，大赦改元，布告其事於天下，築玉清昭應宮。

translations.literal: After the emperor had received the Heavenly Writ, he proclaimed a great amnesty and changed the reign title, announced the matter throughout the realm, and built the Jade Purity Zhaoying Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the Heavenly Writ the emperor proclaimed a great amnesty, changed the reign title, announced the event throughout the realm, and built the Jade Purity Zhaoying Palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天書復降泰山，帝以親受符命，遂議封禪，作禮樂。

translations.literal: That year the Heavenly Writ again descended at Mount Tai; the emperor, because he had personally received the talisman mandate, thereupon deliberated on the Feng and Shan sacrifices and composed ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Heavenly Writ descended again at Mount Tai; Because he had personally received the mandate, the emperor deliberated on the Feng and Shan rites and composed ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 王欽若、陳堯叟、丁謂、杜鎬、陳彭年皆以經義左右附和，由是天下爭言符瑞矣。

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo, Chen Yaosou, Ding Wei, Du Hao, and Chen Pengnian all used classical arguments to support and echo him on left and right, and from this the realm vied to speak of portents and omens.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo, Chen Yaosou, Ding Wei, Du Hao, and Chen Pengnian all used classical learning to echo him, and thereafter the whole realm vied to speak of portents and omens.

sentences.zh: 四年，又將祀汾陰，是時大旱，京師近郡穀踴貴，奭上疏諫曰：「先王卜征，五年歲習其祥，祥習則行，不習則增修德而改卜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was again to sacrifice at Fenyin; at that time there was great drought and grain prices soared in the capital region; Shi submitted a remonstrance, saying: "Former kings divined before a campaign; for five years they practiced the auspicious omen—when the omen was practiced they marched, and when it was not practiced they increased virtue and divined again."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the emperor planned again to sacrifice at Fenyin; a severe drought had driven grain prices sharply higher near the capital; Shi submitted a remonstrance: "Former kings divined before a campaign; for five years they rehearsed the auspicious omen—when the omen was confirmed they marched; when it was not, they cultivated virtue and divined again."

sentences.zh: 陛下始畢東封，更議西幸，殆非先王卜征五年慎重之意，其不可一也。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty has just completed the eastern Feng and now deliberates a western journey—this is scarcely the former kings' meaning in divining for five years with caution; this is the first reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty has just completed the eastern Feng and now plans a western journey—this scarcely matches the former kings' careful five-year divination; this is the first reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 夫汾陰后土，事不經見。

translations.literal: "The Queen Mother of Earth at Fenyin is a matter not found in the classics."
translations.idiomatic: "Sacrifice to the Queen Mother of Earth at Fenyin is not attested in the classics."

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝將封禪，故先封中嶽，祠汾陰，始巡幸郡縣，遂有事於泰山。

translations.literal: "Formerly Emperor Wu of Han, about to perform Feng and Shan, therefore first enfeoffed the central peak and sacrificed at Fenyin, then toured the commanderies and districts, and thereafter undertook affairs at Mount Tai."
translations.idiomatic: "When Emperor Wu of Han prepared the Feng and Shan, he first enfeoffed the central peak and sacrificed at Fenyin, then toured the commanderies, and only afterward performed the rites at Mount Tai."

sentences.zh: 今陛下既已登封，復欲幸汾陰，其不可二也。

translations.literal: "Now Your Majesty has already ascended to perform Feng; to desire again to visit Fenyin is the second reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty has already performed the Feng; to visit Fenyin again is the second reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 古者圜丘方澤，所以郊祀天地，今南北郊是也。

translations.literal: "In antiquity the round mound and square pond were for suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth; the present southern and northern suburbs are this."
translations.idiomatic: "In antiquity the round mound and square pond served to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the suburbs; our present southern and northern suburban altars fulfill that role."

sentences.zh: 漢初承秦，唯立五畤以祀天，而后土無祀，故武帝立祠於汾陰。

translations.literal: "At the beginning of Han, inheriting Qin, they established only the five altars to sacrifice to Heaven; the Queen Mother of Earth had no sacrifice, and therefore Emperor Wu established a shrine at Fenyin."
translations.idiomatic: "Early Han, inheriting Qin, established only the five altars to Heaven; Earth had no shrine, so Emperor Wu established sacrifice to the Queen Mother of Earth at Fenyin."

sentences.zh: 自元、成以來，從公卿之議，遂徙汾陰后土於北郊，後之王者多不祀汾陰。

translations.literal: "From Yuan and Cheng onward, following the deliberations of the dukes and ministers, they moved the Queen Mother of Earth at Fenyin to the northern suburb; later kings mostly did not sacrifice at Fenyin."
translations.idiomatic: "From the Yuan and Cheng reigns onward, following ministerial debate, sacrifice to Earth at Fenyin was moved to the northern suburb; later rulers mostly ceased sacrificing at Fenyin."

sentences.zh: 今陛下已建北郊，乃舍之而遠祀汾陰，其不可三也。

translations.literal: "Now Your Majesty has already established the northern suburb yet abandons it to sacrifice far at Fenyin—this is the third reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty has already established the northern suburban altar yet would abandon it to sacrifice far away at Fenyin—this is the third reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 西漢都雍，去汾陰至近。

translations.literal: "Western Han made its capital at Yong, very near Fenyin."
translations.idiomatic: "Western Han made its capital at Yong, very close to Fenyin."

sentences.zh: 今陛下經重關，越險阻，輕棄京師根本，而慕西漢之虛名，其不可四也。

translations.literal: "Now Your Majesty would pass through many passes and cross dangerous terrain, lightly abandon the capital's foundation, and covet Western Han's empty reputation—this is the fourth reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Now Your Majesty would pass heavy barriers and dangerous terrain, lightly leave the capital's foundation, and covet Western Han's empty reputation—this is the fourth reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 河東，唐王業之所起也。

translations.literal: "Hedong was where the Tang house's enterprise arose."
translations.idiomatic: "Hedong was where the Tang dynasty's enterprise arose."

sentences.zh: 唐又都雍，故明皇間幸河東，因祠后土。

translations.literal: "Tang also made its capital at Yong; therefore Emperor Ming of Tang occasionally visited Hedong and sacrificed to the Queen Mother of Earth."
translations.idiomatic: "Tang also made its capital at Yong; therefore Emperor Ming of Tang occasionally visited Hedong and sacrificed to the Queen Mother of Earth."

sentences.zh: 聖朝之興，事與唐異，而陛下無故欲祀汾陰，其不可五也。

translations.literal: "The rise of our sacred dynasty differs from Tang, yet Your Majesty for no reason wishes to sacrifice at Fenyin—this is the fifth reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Our dynasty's rise differs from Tang's, yet Your Majesty would for no reason sacrifice at Fenyin—this is the fifth reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 昔者周宣王遇災而懼，故詩人美其中興，以為賢主。

translations.literal: "Formerly King Xuan of Zhou encountered disaster and was fearful; therefore the poets praised his restoration as a worthy ruler."
translations.idiomatic: "Formerly King Xuan of Zhou met with disaster and was fearful; the poets therefore praised his restoration as a worthy ruler."

sentences.zh: 比年以來，水旱相繼，陛下宜側身修德，以答天譴，豈宜下徇奸回，遠勞民庶，盤遊不已，忘社稷之大計？

translations.literal: "In recent years flood and drought have followed one another; Your Majesty should turn inward and cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's reproof—how can you instead follow wicked men, far weary the people, and travel without cease, forgetting the great plan of the altars of state?"
translations.idiomatic: "In recent years flood and drought have followed one another; Your Majesty should turn inward and cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's reproof—how can you instead follow wicked advisers, weary the people on distant journeys, and travel without cease, forgetting the state's great foundations?"

sentences.zh: 其不可六也。

translations.literal: "This is the sixth reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "This is the sixth reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 夫雷以二月啟蟄，八月收聲，育養萬物，失時則為異。

translations.literal: "Thunder in the second month awakens the insects; in the eighth month it ceases its sound, nourishing the myriad things—when untimely it is an anomaly."
translations.idiomatic: "Thunder in the second month awakens insects; in the eighth month it ceases, nourishing the myriad creatures—when untimely it is an omen."

sentences.zh: 今震雷在冬，為異尤甚。

translations.literal: "Now thunder in winter is an anomaly still more severe."
translations.idiomatic: "Thunder in winter is an omen still more severe."

sentences.zh: 此天意丁寧以戒陛下，而反未悟，殆失天意，其不可七也。

translations.literal: "This is Heaven's earnest admonition to warn Your Majesty, yet you have not yet understood—almost losing Heaven's intent; this is the seventh reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "This is Heaven earnestly warning Your Majesty, yet you have not understood—nearly missing Heaven's intent; this is the seventh reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 夫民，神之主也，是以聖王先成民而後致力於神。

translations.literal: "The people are the masters of the spirits; therefore sage kings first complete the people and afterward exert effort on the spirits."
translations.idiomatic: "The people are the masters of the spirits; therefore sage kings first secure the people and only then serve the spirits."

sentences.zh: 今國家土木之功累年未息，水旱洊沴，饑饉居多，乃欲勞民事神，神其享之乎？

translations.literal: "Now the state's construction in earth and wood has not ceased for years; flood and drought come repeatedly, famine is widespread, yet you wish to weary the people to serve the spirits—will the spirits enjoy it?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now state construction has not ceased for years; flood and drought recur, famine is widespread—yet you would weary the people to serve the spirits; will the spirits accept such sacrifice?"

sentences.zh: 此其不可八也。

translations.literal: "This is the eighth reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "This is the eighth reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲為此者，不過效漢武帝、唐明皇，巡幸所至，刻石頌功，以崇虛名，誇示後世爾。

translations.literal: "If Your Majesty must do this, it is nothing but imitating Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Ming of Tang—wherever they traveled they carved stone to praise merit, exalting empty reputation to boast to later ages."
