translations.idiomatic: "If Your Majesty insists on doing this, it is nothing but imitating Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Ming of Tang—wherever they went they carved stone to praise their merit and exalt empty fame for posterity."

sentences.zh: 陛下天資聖明，當慕二帝、三王，何為下襲漢、唐之虛名，其不可九也。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty's natural endowment is sagely and bright; you should emulate the Two Emperors and Three Kings—why descend to follow Han and Tang's empty reputation? This is the ninth reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty's nature is sagely and bright; you should emulate the Two Emperors and Three Kings—why descend to follow Han and Tang's empty reputation? This is the ninth reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 唐明皇以嬖寵奸邪，內外交害，身播國屯，兵交關下，亡亂之跡如此，由狃於承平，肆行非義，稔致禍敗。

translations.literal: "Emperor Ming of Tang, through favoring wicked flatterers, suffered harm within and without; his person was cast abroad and the state fell into turmoil, with armies clashing below the passes—the traces of ruin and disorder were such as this, because he was accustomed to long peace and wantonly acted against righteousness until disaster ripened."
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Ming of Tang, through favoring wicked flatterers, suffered harm within and without; he fled abroad and the state fell into turmoil, with armies clashing below the passes—such were the traces of ruin, because accustomed to long peace he wantonly acted against righteousness until disaster ripened."

sentences.zh: 今議者引開元故事以為盛烈，乃欲倡導陛下而為之，臣切為陛下不取，此其不可十也。

translations.literal: "Now deliberators cite the Kaiyuan precedent as a great achievement and wish to lead Your Majesty to do the same; your subject is deeply convinced this should not be taken—this is the tenth reason it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Now advisers cite the Kaiyuan precedent as a great achievement and wish to lead Your Majesty to follow it; I am deeply convinced Your Majesty should not do so—this is the tenth reason it should not be done."

sentences.zh: 臣言不逮意，陛下以臣言為可取，願少賜清問，以畢臣說。」

translations.literal: "Your subject's words do not reach his meaning; if Your Majesty finds your subject's words acceptable, I wish you would grant a little clear inquiry to complete your subject's exposition.""
translations.idiomatic: "My words may not fully express my meaning; if Your Majesty finds them acceptable, I beg a little further questioning so that I may complete my argument.""

sentences.zh: 帝遣內侍皇甫繼明就問，又上疏曰：

translations.literal: The emperor sent the inner attendant Huangfu Jiming to inquire of him, and he again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the inner attendant Huangfu Jiming to question him, and Shi submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 陛下將幸汾陰，而京師民心弗寧，江、淮之眾困於調發，理須鎮安而矜存之。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty is about to visit Fenyin, yet the hearts of the people in the capital are unsettled, and the masses of the Jiang and Huai regions are distressed by requisitions—it is right to pacify and cherish them."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty plans to visit Fenyin, yet the capital populace is uneasy and the people of the Jiang and Huai regions are exhausted by levies—you should pacify and relieve them."

sentences.zh: 且土木之功未息，而奪攘之盜公行，外國治兵，不遠邊境，使者雖至，寧可保其心乎？

translations.literal: "Moreover, construction in earth and wood has not ceased, while robbers who seize and plunder walk openly; foreign states drill troops not far from the borders—though envoys arrive, can their hearts be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: "Construction has not ceased, bandits roam openly, and foreign states drill troops near the borders—though envoys come, can we trust their intentions?"

sentences.zh: 昔陳勝起於徭戍，黃巢出於凶饑，隋煬帝勤遠略而唐高祖興於晉陽，晉少主惑小人而耶律德光長驅中國。

translations.literal: "Formerly Chen Sheng arose from corvée garrison duty, Huang Chao emerged from severe famine; Emperor Yang of Sui pursued far-reaching strategy while Tang Gaozu rose at Jinyang; the young lord of Jin was deluded by petty men while Yelü Deguang drove deep into China."
translations.idiomatic: "Chen Sheng rose from corvée labor, Huang Chao from famine; Emperor Yang of Sui pursued distant campaigns while Tang Gaozu rose at Jinyang; the Jin young lord was misled by petty men while Yelü Deguang swept deep into China."

sentences.zh: 陛下俯從奸佞，遠棄京師，涉仍歲薦饑之墟，修違經久廢之祠，不念民疲，不恤邊患。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty bows to follow wicked flatterers, abandons the capital far away, crosses lands of repeated famine and sacrifice, repairs shrines long abandoned contrary to the classics, and does not consider the people's exhaustion or pity border troubles."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty follows wicked flatterers, abandons the capital, crosses lands of repeated famine, restores long-abandoned shrines contrary to the classics, and ignores the people's exhaustion and border dangers."

sentences.zh: 安知今日戍卒無陳勝，饑民無黃巢，英雄將無窺伺於肘腋，外敵將無觀釁於邊陲乎？

translations.literal: "How do you know that among today's garrison soldiers there is no Chen Sheng, among the hungry no Huang Chao, among heroes no one watching for opportunity at your elbow, among foreign enemies no one watching for a breach at the frontier?"
translations.idiomatic: "Who can say today's garrison soldiers hold no Chen Sheng, the hungry no Huang Chao, ambitious men no designs at your elbow, or foreign enemies no designs on the borders?"

sentences.zh: 先帝嘗議封禪，寅畏天災，尋詔停寢。

translations.literal: "The former emperor once deliberated on Feng and Shan, feared Heaven's calamities, and soon ordered the plan halted."
translations.idiomatic: "The former emperor once considered Feng and Shan but, in awe of Heaven's calamities, soon ordered the plan suspended."

sentences.zh: 今奸臣乃讚陛下力行東封，以為繼成先誌。

translations.literal: "Now wicked ministers praise Your Majesty for vigorously undertaking the eastern Feng, taking it as continuing and completing the former emperor's intent."
translations.idiomatic: "Now wicked ministers praise Your Majesty for pressing ahead with the eastern Feng as fulfilling the former emperor's intent."

sentences.zh: 先帝嘗欲北平幽朔，西取繼遷，大勳未集，用付陛下，則群臣未嘗獻一謀、畫一策，以佐陛下繼先帝之志者，反務卑辭重幣，求和於契丹，蹙國縻爵，姑息於繼遷，曾不思主辱臣死為可戒，誣下罔上為可羞。

translations.literal: "The former emperor once wished to pacify the north and recover Youzhou in the west; great merit was not gathered and the task was entrusted to Your Majesty—yet the ministers never offered one plan or one stratagem to help Your Majesty continue the former emperor's intent; instead they busied themselves with humble words and heavy gifts, seeking peace with the Khitan, shrinking the state and binding titles, indulging Li Jiqian, never thinking that the lord's disgrace and the minister's death were a warning, or that deceiving superiors and misleading the realm was shameful."
translations.idiomatic: "The former emperor wished to pacify the north and recover Youzhou; the great task was left to Your Majesty—yet ministers never offered a single plan to continue that intent, instead seeking peace with the Khitan through humble gifts, shrinking the state and indulging Li Jiqian, never remembering that a minister should die for his lord's disgrace or that deceiving the throne is shameful."

sentences.zh: 撰造祥瑞，假托鬼神，才畢東封，便議西幸，輕勞車駕，虐害饑民，冀其無事往還，便謂成大勳績。

translations.literal: "They fabricated auspicious omens and falsely invoked spirits; scarcely had the eastern Feng ended when they deliberated a western journey, lightly troubling the imperial carriage and cruelly harming the hungry people, hoping that if nothing happened on the journey back and forth they could call it a great achievement."
translations.idiomatic: "They fabricated omens and invoked spirits falsely; scarcely had the eastern Feng ended when they planned a western journey, lightly troubling the imperial procession and cruelly harming the hungry, hoping a safe round trip would count as great achievement."

sentences.zh: 是陛下以祖宗艱難之業，為奸邪僥幸之資，臣所以長歎而痛哭也。

translations.literal: "Thus Your Majesty makes the ancestors' hard-won enterprise the resource of wicked men's lucky striving—this is why your subject sighs long and weeps."
translations.idiomatic: "Thus Your Majesty turns the ancestors' hard-won enterprise into wicked men's opportunity for lucky gain—this is why I sigh and weep."

sentences.zh: 夫天地神祇，聰明正直，作善降之百祥，作不善降之百殃，未聞專事籩豆簠簋，可邀福祥。

translations.literal: "Heaven and Earth and the spirits are intelligent, upright, and bright; doing good brings a hundred blessings, doing evil a hundred calamities—never have I heard that by serving only with baskets and vessels one can invite fortune."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven, Earth, and the spirits are intelligent and upright; good brings blessings, evil calamities—never have I heard that ritual vessels alone can win fortune."

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「國之將興，聽於民；

translations.literal: "The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: "When a state is about to rise, it listens to the people;"
translations.idiomatic: "The Zuo Commentary says, "When a state is about to rise, it listens to the people;"

sentences.zh: 將亡，聽於神。

translations.literal: "when it is about to perish, it listens to the spirits.""
translations.idiomatic: "when it is about to fall, it heeds the spirits instead.""

sentences.zh: 」愚臣非敢妄議，惟陛下終賜裁擇。

translations.literal: "Your foolish subject does not dare speak rashly; only may Your Majesty finally grant judgment and choice.""
translations.idiomatic: "I dare not speak rashly; I only ask that Your Majesty judge and choose wisely.""

sentences.zh: 後天下數有災變，又言：「古者五載巡守，有國之事爾，非必有紫氣黃雲，然後登封，嘉禾異草，然後省方也。

translations.literal: "Afterward calamities and anomalies repeatedly occurred in the realm, and he again said: "In antiquity the five-year tour of inspection was a matter for rulers with a state—not that there must be purple vapor and yellow clouds before ascending to Feng, or fine grain and strange plants before visiting the regions."
translations.idiomatic: "Later calamities recurred throughout the realm, and he again said: "The five-year tour of inspection was a ruler's duty—not that purple vapor and yellow clouds must precede the Feng, or miraculous grain before touring the regions."

sentences.zh: 今野雕山鹿，郡國交奏，秋旱冬雷，群臣率賀，退而腹非竊笑者比比皆是。

translations.literal: "Now wild eagles and mountain deer are reported from the commanderies and prefectures; autumn drought and winter thunder—ministers all congratulate, yet those who withdraw and secretly laugh in their bellies are everywhere."
translations.idiomatic: "Now wild eagles and mountain deer are reported everywhere; autumn drought and winter thunder—and ministers congratulate while countless men withdraw to mock in secret."

sentences.zh: 孰謂上天為可罔，下民為可愚，後世為可欺乎？

translations.literal: "Who says Heaven can be deceived, the people fooled, or posterity cheated?"
translations.idiomatic: "Who believes Heaven can be deceived, the people fooled, or posterity cheated?"

sentences.zh: 人情如此，所損不細，惟陛下深鑒其妄。」

translations.literal: "Human sentiment being thus, the harm is no small matter—only may Your Majesty deeply discern its falsity.""
translations.idiomatic: "Sentiment being thus, the harm is great—may Your Majesty deeply discern its falsity.""

sentences.zh: 六年，又上疏曰：「陛下封泰山，祀汾陰，躬謁陵寢，今又將祠於太清宮，外議籍籍，以謂陛下事事慕效唐明皇，豈以明皇為令德之主耶？

translations.literal: "In the sixth year he again submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty performed Feng at Mount Tai, sacrificed at Fenyin, personally visited the imperial tombs, and now will again sacrifice at the Great Pure Palace; outside talk is clamorous, saying Your Majesty in everything imitates Tang Emperor Ming—do you take Emperor Ming as a ruler of fine virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: "In the sixth year he memorialized again: "Your Majesty performed Feng at Mount Tai, sacrificed at Fenyin, visited the tombs, and now will sacrifice at the Great Pure Palace; public talk says you imitate Tang Emperor Ming in everything—do you take Ming as a ruler of fine virtue?"

sentences.zh: 甚不然也。

translations.literal: "That is very much not so."
translations.idiomatic: "That is far from true."

sentences.zh: 明皇禍敗之跡有足為深戒者，非獨臣能知之，近臣不言者，此懷奸以事陛下也。

translations.literal: "Emperor Ming's traces of disaster and ruin are sufficient as a deep warning—not only your subject knows this; that nearby ministers do not speak is because they harbor wickedness in serving Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: "Ming's path to ruin is warning enough—not only I know it; that nearby ministers stay silent shows they serve Your Majesty with wicked intent."

sentences.zh: 明皇之無道，亦無敢言者，及奔至馬嵬，軍士已誅楊國忠，請矯詔之罪，乃始諭以識理不明，寄任失所。

translations.literal: "None dared speak of Emperor Ming's want of the Way; only when he fled to Mawei and the soldiers had already executed Yang Guozhong and requested punishment under a forged edict did he begin to acknowledge unclear understanding and misplaced trust."
translations.idiomatic: "None dared speak of Ming's misconduct; only at Mawei, after the soldiers killed Yang Guozhong, did he acknowledge confused judgment and misplaced trust."

sentences.zh: 當時雖有罪己之言，覺寤已晚，何所及也。

translations.literal: "Though at the time there were words of self-reproach, awakening came too late—what could be done?"
translations.idiomatic: "Though he spoke of fault then, awakening came too late—what good did it do?"

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下早自覺寤，抑損虛華，斥遠邪佞，罷興土木，不襲危亂之跡，無為明皇不及之悔，此天下之幸，社稷之福也。

translations.literal: "Your subject wishes Your Majesty to awaken early, restrain empty display, drive away wicked flatterers, cease construction in earth and wood, not follow traces of peril and disorder, and have no regret that you fell short of Emperor Ming—this would be the fortune of the realm and the blessing of the altars of state.""
translations.idiomatic: "I wish Your Majesty to awaken early, restrain empty display, drive away flatterers, cease construction, avoid paths to chaos, and escape Ming's regret—this would bless the realm and the state.""

sentences.zh: 」帝以為「封泰山，祠汾陰，上陵，祀老子，非始於明皇。

translations.literal: "The emperor considered that "Feng at Mount Tai, sacrifice at Fenyin, visiting the tombs, and sacrificing to Laozi did not begin with Emperor Ming."
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor replied that Feng at Mount Tai, sacrifice at Fenyin, tomb visits, and sacrifice to Laozi did not begin with Emperor Ming."

sentences.zh: 《開元禮》今世所循用，不可以天寶之亂，舉謂為非也。

translations.literal: "The Kaiyuan Rites are what the present age follows—one cannot because of the Tianbao disorder declare them wrong."
translations.idiomatic: "The Kaiyuan Rites are what we follow today—one cannot reject them because of the Tianbao disorders."

sentences.zh: 秦為無道甚矣，今官名、詔妙、郡縣猶襲秦舊，豈以人而廢言乎？

translations.literal: "Qin was utterly without the Way, yet today office titles, edict phrasing, and commanderies and districts still follow Qin old forms—how can one reject words because of the man?"
translations.idiomatic: "Qin was utterly lawless, yet we still follow Qin forms in titles and administration—how reject a teaching because of the teacher?"

sentences.zh: 」作《解疑論》以示群臣。

translations.literal: "He composed Clarifying Doubts to show the ministers."
translations.idiomatic: "He composed Clarifying Doubts to show his ministers."

sentences.zh: 然知奭樸忠，雖其言切直，容之而弗斥。

translations.literal: "Yet knowing Shi's plain loyalty, though his words were blunt and direct, he tolerated him and did not rebuke him."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet knowing Shi's plain loyalty, though his words were blunt, the emperor tolerated him without rebuke."

sentences.zh: 久之，以父老請歸田里，不許，以知密州。

translations.literal: "After a long time, because the local elders requested that he return to his home district, permission was not granted, and he was appointed prefect of Mizhou."
translations.idiomatic: "After a time, when hometown elders petitioned for him to retire to his fields, the court refused and instead made him prefect of Mizhou."

sentences.zh: 居二年，遷左諫議大夫，罷待制。

translations.literal: "After two years he was promoted to Left Remonstrator and removed from his pending appointment."
translations.idiomatic: "After two years he was made left remonstrator and removed from his court appointment."

sentences.zh: 還，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: "On return he investigated capital criminal cases."
translations.idiomatic: "On returning to court he investigated capital criminal cases."

sentences.zh: 是時初置天慶、天祺、天貺、先天、降聖節，天下設齋醮張燕，費甚廣。

translations.literal: "At that time the Tianqing, Tianqi, Tiankuang, Xiantian, and Jiangsheng festivals were first established; throughout the realm fasting, libations, and banquets were held at great expense."
translations.idiomatic: "At that time the Tianqing and related festivals were established; the realm held costly fasts and banquets."

sentences.zh: 奭又請裁省浮用，不報。

translations.literal: "Shi again requested reduction of extravagant expenditure; there was no reply."
translations.idiomatic: "Shi again asked to cut extravagant spending; the court did not reply."

sentences.zh: 復出知河陽，又求解官就養，遷給事中，徙兗州。

translations.literal: "He went out again as prefect of Heyang, again requested dismissal to care for his parents, was moved to Supervising Censor, and transferred to Yanzhou."
translations.idiomatic: "He served again as prefect of Heyang, asked to retire to care for his parents, was made supervising censor, then transferred to Yanzhou."

sentences.zh: 天禧中，朱能獻《乾祐天書》。

translations.literal: "In the Tianxi period Zhu Neng presented the Qianyou Heavenly Writ."
translations.idiomatic: "In Tianxi, Zhu Neng presented the Qianyou Heavenly Writ."

sentences.zh: 復上疏曰：

translations.literal: "He again submitted a memorial, saying:"
translations.idiomatic: "He submitted another memorial:"

sentences.zh: 朱能者，奸憸小人，妄言祥瑞，而陛下崇信之，屈至尊以迎拜，歸秘殿以奉安，上自朝廷，下及閭巷，靡不痛心疾首，反唇腹非，而無敢言者。

translations.literal: "Zhu Neng is a wicked, crafty petty man who falsely speaks of auspicious omens, yet Your Majesty honors and trusts him, bending the supreme dignity to go forth and receive him in obeisance and returning him to the secret hall for installation—from the court above to the lanes below none do not ache in heart and turn their lips in secret despite, yet none dare speak."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhu Neng is a wicked petty man who fabricates omens, yet Your Majesty honors him, bending imperial dignity to receive him and installing the writ in the secret hall—from court to marketplace all ache in heart and curse in secret, yet none dare speak."

sentences.zh: 昔漢文成將軍以帛書飯牛，既而言牛腹中有奇書，殺視得書，天子識其手跡。

translations.literal: "Formerly the Han Literary and Martial generals fed a cow silk books; afterward they said there was a strange book in the cow's belly; killing and viewing it they obtained the book, and the Son of Heaven recognized the handwriting."
translations.idiomatic: "Formerly Han's Literary and Martial generals fed a cow silk texts, then claimed a miraculous book lay in its belly; when the beast was killed and opened, the emperor recognized the handwriting."

sentences.zh: 又有五利將軍妄言，方多不仇，二人皆坐誅。

translations.literal: "There was also the Five Benefits general who spoke rashly; in many ways they did not agree—both were convicted and executed."
translations.idiomatic: "The Five Benefits general also spoke rashly and was executed with him."

sentences.zh: 先帝時有侯莫陳利用者，以方術暴得寵用，一旦發其奸，誅於鄭州。

translations.literal: "In the former emperor's time there was Hou Mochan Liyong, who through occult arts suddenly gained favor; once his wickedness was exposed he was executed at Zhengzhou."
translations.idiomatic: "Under the former emperor Hou Mochan Liyong gained favor through occult arts; once exposed he was executed at Zhengzhou."

sentences.zh: 漢武可謂雄材，先帝可謂英斷。

translations.literal: "Emperor Wu of Han may be called heroic in talent; the former emperor may be called decisively brilliant."
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Wu of Han was heroic; the former emperor was decisively brilliant."

sentences.zh: 唐明皇得《靈寶符》、《上清護國經》、《寶券》等，皆王鉷、田同秀等所為，明皇不能顯戮，怵於邪說，自謂德實動天，神必福我。

translations.literal: "Tang Emperor Ming obtained the Lingbao talisman, the Protect-the-State scripture of the Upper Clarity, treasure bonds, and the like—all made by Wang Hong, Tian Tongxiu, and others; Emperor Ming could not openly execute them but was cowed by heterodox teachings, himself thinking his virtue had moved Heaven and the spirits must bless him."
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Ming obtained the Lingbao talisman and similar texts—all forged by Wang Hong and Tian Tongxiu; Ming could not punish them openly but was cowed by heterodoxy, thinking Heaven must bless him."

sentences.zh: 夫老君，聖人也。

translations.literal: "Now Lord Lao was a sage."
translations.idiomatic: "Lord Lao, after all, was a sage."

sentences.zh: 倘實降語，固宜不妄，而唐自安、史亂離，乘輿播越，兩都蕩覆，四海沸騰，豈天下太平乎？

translations.literal: "If he truly descended with words, they should certainly not be reckless—yet Tang from the An and Shi disorders, the imperial carriage cast about, both capitals overthrown and the realm boiling—was the realm at peace?"
translations.idiomatic: "If he truly spoke from Heaven, his words should not be reckless—yet from the An-Shi rebellion both capitals fell and the realm boiled—was that peace?"

sentences.zh: 明皇雖僅得歸闕，復為李輔國劫遷，卒以憂終，豈聖壽無疆、長生久視乎？

translations.literal: "Emperor Ming though he barely returned to the palace was again seized and moved by Li Fuguo, ending in sorrow—was his sage longevity without limit or his vision of long life?"
translations.idiomatic: "Ming barely returned to the palace, was seized by Li Fuguo, and died in grief—was that sage longevity?"

sentences.zh: 以明皇之英睿，而禍患猥至曾不知者，良由在位既久，驕亢成性，謂人莫己若，謂諫不足聽＃心玩居常之安，耳熟導諛之說，內惑寵嬖，外任奸回，曲奉鬼神，過崇妖妄。

translations.literal: "With Emperor Ming's brilliance, calamities came in swarms yet he did not know—truly because having long held office he became proud, thinking none equal to himself, thinking remonstrance not worth hearing, playing with constant ease, ears accustomed to flattery, inwardly deluded by favorites, outwardly trusting wicked men, crookedly serving ghosts and spirits and excessively honoring demonic falsity."
translations.idiomatic: "With Ming's brilliance, calamity came yet he did not know—because long in power he grew proud, disdained remonstrance, delighted in ease, heard only flattery, favored concubines, trusted wicked men, and worshipped demons."

sentences.zh: 今日見老君於閣上，明日見老君於山中。

translations.literal: "Today seeing Lord Lao in the pavilion, tomorrow seeing Lord Lao in the mountains."
translations.idiomatic: "Today Lord Lao appeared in the pavilion, tomorrow in the mountains."

sentences.zh: 大臣屍祿以將迎，端士畏威而緘默。

translations.literal: "Great ministers held salary and went to welcome; upright gentlemen feared authority and kept silent."
translations.idiomatic: "Great ministers drew salary and went to welcome; upright men feared authority and kept silent."

sentences.zh: 既惑左道，既紊政經，民心用離，變起倉卒。

translations.literal: "Already deluded by the left Way, already disordering government constants—the people's hearts departed and sudden change arose."
translations.idiomatic: "Deluded by heterodoxy and disordering government, the people's hearts departed and sudden rebellion arose."

sentences.zh: 當是之時，老君寧肯禦兵，寶符安能排蒲邪？

translations.literal: "At that time did Lord Lao deign to ward off troops? Could the treasure talisman repel the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: "Then did Lord Lao ward off troops? Could a talisman repel the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 今朱能所為，或類於此，願陛下思漢武之雄材，法先帝之英斷，鑒明皇之蹤禍，庶幾災害不生，禍亂不作。

translations.literal: "Now what Zhu Neng does may resemble this; I wish Your Majesty would reflect on Emperor Wu's heroic talent, follow the former emperor's decisive brilliance, and take warning from Emperor Ming's traces of calamity, so that disasters and disorder may not arise."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhu Neng's conduct resembles this; may Your Majesty emulate Han Wu's talent, the former emperor's decisiveness, and Ming's warning, so disaster does not arise."

sentences.zh: 未幾，能果敗。

translations.literal: "Before long Neng indeed failed."
translations.idiomatic: "Soon Neng indeed failed."

sentences.zh: 奭又嘗請減修寺度僧，帝雖未用其言，嘗令向敏中諭令陳時政訪失奭以納諫、恕直、輕徭、薄斂四事為言，頗施行焉。

translations.literal: "Shi also once requested reducing temple construction and ordaining monks; though the emperor did not use his words, he once had Xiang Minzhong instruct him to present current policy and errors—Shi spoke on accepting remonstrance, pardoning blunt speech, light corvée, and low levies, and many were implemented."
translations.idiomatic: "Shi also asked to reduce temple building and ordinations; though the emperor did not adopt this, he had Xiang Minzhong solicit policy advice—Shi spoke on accepting remonstrance, pardoning blunt speech, light corvée, and low levies, and much was implemented."

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，宰相請擇名儒以經術侍講讀，乃召為翰林侍講學士、知審官院，判機子監，修《真宗實錄》。

translations.literal: "When Renzong took the throne the chief ministers requested selecting renowned Confucians to attend in classical learning for lectures and reading; he was summoned as Hanlin Lecturer and Academician, knew the Bureau of Review, judged the Directorate of Astronomy, and compiled the Veritable Records of Zhenzong."
translations.idiomatic: "When Renzong succeeded, ministers chose renowned Confucians for the heir's instruction; Shi was summoned as Hanlin lecturer, directed the Bureau of Review, judged the Directorate of Astronomy, and compiled Zhenzong's Veritable Records."

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起復，兼判太常寺及禮院，三遷兵部侍郎、龍霞閣學士。

translations.literal: "Upon his father's death he was recalled to office, concurrently judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ritual Court, and was thrice promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Academic Scholar of the Dragon Glow Hall."
translations.idiomatic: "On his father's death he was recalled from mourning, concurrently judged ritual courts, and was thrice promoted to vice director of war and academician of the Dragon Glow Hall."

sentences.zh: 每講論至前世亂君亡國，必反覆規諷。

translations.literal: "Whenever in lecturing he reached former-age disorderly rulers and perished states he always turned back to admonish repeatedly."
translations.idiomatic: "Whenever his lectures reached tyrants and fallen states he admonished repeatedly."

sentences.zh: 仁宗意或不在書，昺則拱默以俟，帝為竦然改聽。

translations.literal: "When Renzong's mind was sometimes not on the book, Bing would bow in silence and wait, and the emperor would start and change to listen."
translations.idiomatic: "When Renzong's attention wandered, Xing Bing would wait in reverent silence until the emperor started and listened again."

sentences.zh: 嘗畫《無逸圖》上之，帝施於講讀閣。

translations.literal: "He once painted the No Dissipation illustration and presented it; the emperor hung it in the lecture hall."
translations.idiomatic: "He once painted and presented the No Dissipation illustration, which the emperor hung in the lecture hall."

sentences.zh: 時章憲明肅皇后每五收一御殿，與帝同聽政，奭言：「古帝王朝朝暮夕，未有曠日不朝。

translations.literal: "At that time Empress Zhangxian Mingsu every fifth day attended court once with the emperor to hear government; Shi said: "Ancient emperors and kings attended morning and evening—there was none who failed to attend court for a whole day."
translations.idiomatic: "When Empress Zhangxian attended court every fifth day, Shi said, "Ancient rulers held court morning and evening—none skipped daily audience."

sentences.zh: 陛下宜每日御殿，以覽萬機。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty should daily attend court to survey the myriad affairs."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty should attend court daily to handle affairs."

sentences.zh: 」奏留中不報。

translations.literal: "The memorial was retained in the palace without reply."
translations.idiomatic: "The memorial was retained without reply."

sentences.zh: 然帝與皇太后尤愛重之，每進見，未嘗不加禮。

translations.literal: "Yet the emperor and empress dowager especially loved and honored him; whenever he entered audience they never failed to add ritual."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the emperor and empress dowager especially honored him; he always received added ceremony on audience."

sentences.zh: 三請致仕。

translations.literal: "Thrice he requested retirement."
translations.idiomatic: "He thrice requested retirement."

sentences.zh: 召對承明殿，敦諭之，以年逾七十固請，泣下，帝亦惻然，詔與馮知講《老子》三章，各賜帛二百匹。

translations.literal: "Summoned to audience at the Chenming Hall, they earnestly instructed him; as he was over seventy he firmly requested it, weeping; the emperor also was moved and ordered him and Feng Zhi to lecture on three chapters of the Laozi, each bestowing two hundred bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: "Summoned to the Chenming Hall and earnestly urged to stay, he wept and firmly requested retirement at over seventy; the emperor was moved and had him and Feng Zhi lecture on three chapters of the Laozi, each receiving two hundred bolts of silk."

sentences.zh: 以不得請，求近郡，優拜工部尚書，復知兗州。

translations.literal: "As he could not obtain his request he asked for a nearby prefecture and was graciously promoted to Minister of Works, again made prefect of Yanzhou."
translations.idiomatic: "Denied retirement, he asked for a nearby post and was graciously made Minister of Works and again prefect of Yanzhou."

sentences.zh: 詔須宴而後行，又留數月，特宴太清樓，近臣皆預，帝作飛白大字以賜二府，而小字賜諸學生，獨奭與晁迥兼賜大小字。

translations.literal: "An edict required a banquet before departure; he was detained several months more and specially banqueted at the Taiqing Tower; nearby ministers all attended; the emperor composed flying-white large characters to bestow on the two departments and small characters on the students—only Shi and Chao Yuan received both large and small."
translations.idiomatic: "Ordered to banquet before leaving, he was detained months more for a banquet at the Taiqing Tower; the emperor gave large flying-white characters to the two departments and small characters to students—only Shi and Chao Yuan received both."

sentences.zh: 詔群臣即席賦詩，太后又別出禁中卒器勸酒。

translations.literal: "An edict ordered all ministers to compose poems on the spot; the empress dowager separately produced forbidden-store vessels to urge wine."
translations.idiomatic: "All ministers were ordered to compose poems on the spot; the empress dowager sent palace vessels to urge wine."

sentences.zh: 翌日，奭入謝，又命講《老子》，賜襲衣、金帶、銀鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: "The next day Shi entered to give thanks and was again ordered to lecture on the Laozi, bestowed court robes, gold belt, and silver saddle and bridle horse."
translations.idiomatic: "The next day he thanked the throne and lectured again on the Laozi, receiving court robes, a gold belt, and a silver-saddled horse."

sentences.zh: 及行，賜隅瑞聖園，又賜詩，詔近臣皆賦。

translations.literal: "On departure he was granted a corner of the Ruicheng Garden and again bestowed a poem; an edict ordered nearby ministers all to compose."
translations.idiomatic: "On departure he received a corner of the Ruicheng Garden and a poem; nearby ministers were ordered to compose in reply."

sentences.zh: 以恭謝恩改禮部尚書，既而累表乞歸，以太子速傅致仕。

translations.literal: "In gratitude for the favor he was changed to Minister of Rites; afterward he repeatedly memorialized begging to return and retired as Tutor of the Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: "In gratitude he was made Minister of Rites; later he repeatedly begged to return and retired as tutor of the heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 疾甚，徙正寢，屏婢妾，謂子瑜曰：「無令我死婦人之手。

translations.literal: "When gravely ill he moved to the main chamber, dismissed maidservants, and said to his son Yu: "Do not let me die by women's hands."
translations.idiomatic: "Gravely ill, he moved to the main chamber, dismissed maidservants, and told his son Yu, "Do not let me die in women's hands."

translations.literal: "He died."
translations.idiomatic: "And so he died."

sentences.zh: 奏至，帝謂張士遜曰：「朕方欲召奭還，而奭遂死矣。

translations.literal: "When the memorial arrived the emperor said to Zhang Shisun: "I was just about to summon Shi back, and Shi has died."
translations.idiomatic: "When word arrived the emperor told Zhang Shisun, "I was about to recall Shi, and he has died."

sentences.zh: 」嗟惜者久之，罷朝一日，贈左僕射，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: "He sighed in regret for a long time, suspended court one day, and posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with posthumous title Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: "He sighed long in regret, suspended court one day, and posthumously made him left vice director with the posthumous title Xuan."

sentences.zh: 奭性方重，事親篤孝。

translations.literal: "Shi's nature was square and weighty; in serving his parents he was deeply filial."
translations.idiomatic: "Shi was upright and grave and deeply filial toward his parents."

sentences.zh: 父亡，舐其面以代頮。

translations.literal: "When his father died he licked his face to replace the washing."
translations.idiomatic: "When his father died he licked his face in place of the ritual washing."

sentences.zh: 常掇《五經》切於治道者，為《經典徽言》五十卷。

translations.literal: "He often gathered passages from the Five Classics bearing on government and made Essential Words of the Classics in fifty scrolls."
translations.idiomatic: "He gathered passages from the Five Classics bearing on government into Essential Words of the Classics in fifty scrolls."

sentences.zh: 又撰《崇祀錄》、《樂記圖》、《五經節解》、《五服制度》。

translations.literal: "He also compiled Records of Honored Sacrifice, Illustrations of Music, Sectional Explanations of the Five Classics, and the Five-Ranks System."
translations.idiomatic: "He also wrote Records of Honored Sacrifice, Illustrations of Music, Sectional Explanations of the Five Classics, and the Five-Ranks System of Mourning."

sentences.zh: 嘗奉詔與邢昺、杜鎬校定諸經正義，《莊子》、《爾雅》釋文，考正《尚書》、《論語》、《孝經》、《爾雅》謬誤及律音義。

translations.literal: "He once received an edict with Xing Bing and Du Hao to collate the authoritative exegeses of the classics, commentaries on the Zhuangzi and Erya, and to correct errors in the Documents, Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, and Erya and in the pronunciation of the law."
translations.idiomatic: "He received an edict with Xing Bing and Du Hao to collate classic exegeses, commentaries on the Zhuangzi and Erya, and correct errors in the Documents, Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, Erya, and legal pronunciations."

sentences.zh: 初，圜丘無外壝，五郊從祀不設席，尊不施冪；

translations.literal: "Formerly the round altar had no outer enclosure, the five suburbs had no mats in accompanying sacrifice, and the vessels had no covers;
translations.idiomatic: "Formerly the round altar lacked an outer enclosure, the five suburbs had no mats in accompanying sacrifice, and vessels had no covers;

sentences.zh: 七祠時饗飲福用一尊，不設數登，升歌不以《雍》徹；

translations.literal: the seven shrines in seasonal feasting used one vessel for drinking blessing and did not set multiple platters; ascending song did not use Yong for withdrawal;
translations.idiomatic: "the seven shrines used one vessel for the blessing cup without multiple platters; ascending song did not use Yong for withdrawal;

sentences.zh: 冬至攝祀昊天上帝，外級止十七位，而不以星辰從；

translations.literal: at the winter solstice the acting sacrifice to August Heaven had only seventeen positions on the outer tier and did not include the stars;
translations.idiomatic: "at the winter solstice the acting sacrifice to August Heaven had only seventeen outer positions without the stars;

sentences.zh: 饗先農在祈穀之前；

translations.literal: feasting the former agriculture came before praying for grain;
translations.idiomatic: "feasting the former agriculture came before praying for grain;

sentences.zh: 上丁釋奠無三獻；

translations.literal: on the upper ding the libation sacrifice had no three presentations;
translations.idiomatic: "on the upper ding the libation sacrifice had no three presentations;

sentences.zh: 宗廟不備二舞；

translations.literal: the ancestral temple did not complete the two dances;
translations.idiomatic: "the ancestral temple lacked the two dances;

sentences.zh: 諸臣當諡者，或既葬乃請。

translations.literal: for ministers due posthumous titles, some requested only after burial."
translations.idiomatic: "ministers due posthumous titles sometimes requested them only after burial."

sentences.zh: 奭吭援古奏正，遂著於禮。

translations.literal: "Shi cited antiquity and memorialized corrections, and they were thereupon set down in ritual."
translations.idiomatic: "Shi cited antiquity and corrected these, and they were written into ritual."

sentences.zh: 又請冬至罷祀五帝，大雩設五帝而罷祠昊天上帝。

translations.literal: "He also requested that at the winter solstice sacrifice to the Five Emperors cease, and that at the great rain prayer the Five Emperors be set up and sacrifice to August Heaven cease."
translations.idiomatic: "He also asked to cease winter-solstice sacrifice to the Five Emperors and at the great rain prayer to set up the Five Emperors while ceasing sacrifice to August Heaven."

sentences.zh: 事下有司議，不合而止。

translations.literal: "The matter was referred to the appropriate offices for deliberation; it did not agree and stopped."
translations.idiomatic: "The matter was referred to the offices; it did not pass and was dropped."

sentences.zh: 瑜，官至工部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: "Yu reached Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and retired."
translations.idiomatic: "Yu rose to vice director of works and retired."

sentences.zh: 王昭素

translations.literal: Wang Zhaosu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhaosu.

sentences.zh: 王昭素，開封酸棗人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhaosu was a man of Suanzao in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhaosu was from Suanzao in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少篤學不仕，有至行，為鄉里所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was devoted to learning and did not take office; he had utmost conduct and was praised by his village.
translations.idiomatic: "As a youth he devoted himself to learning and never took office; his conduct was exemplary and his village praised him."

sentences.zh: 常聚徒教授以自給，李穆與弟肅及李惲皆常師事焉。

translations.literal: He often gathered disciples to teach for his livelihood; Li Mu and his younger brother Su and Li Yun all regularly took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: "He supported himself by teaching disciples; Li Mu, his brother Su, and Li Yun were all his students."

sentences.zh: 鄉人爭訟，不詣官府，多就昭素決之。

translations.literal: When villagers had disputes they did not go to the government offices but mostly came to Zhaosu for decision.
translations.idiomatic: "Villagers in dispute did not go to the magistrate but came to Zhaosu for judgment."

sentences.zh: 昭素博通《九經》，兼究《莊》、《老》，尤精《詩》、《易》，以為王、韓注《易》及孔、馬疏義或未盡是，乃著《易論》二十三篇。

translations.literal: Zhaosu was comprehensively versed in the Nine Classics and also investigated the Zhuangzi and Laozi; he was especially skilled in the Classic of Poetry (Shi) and the Classic of Changes (Yi), considering that Wang Bi's and Han Kangbo's commentaries on the Changes and the Kong and Ma exegeses were not entirely correct, and therefore composed Discussions on the Changes in twenty-three chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosu mastered the Nine Classics and also studied the Zhuangzi and Laozi; he was especially adept in the Book of Poetry and the Book of Changes, held that Wang Bi's and Han Kangbo's commentaries on the Changes and the Kong and Ma exegeses were not entirely correct, and wrote Discussions on the Changes in twenty-three chapters.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，穆薦之朝，詔召赴闕，見於便殿，時年七十七，精神不衰。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao period Mu recommended him to court; an edict summoned him to the capital; he was received in the side hall; at the time he was seventy-seven and his spirit was undiminished.
translations.idiomatic: "In Kaibao, Mu recommended him to court; he was summoned to the capital and received in the side hall at seventy-seven, his spirit undiminished."

sentences.zh: 太祖問曰：「何以不求仕進，致相見之晚？

translations.literal: Taizu asked: "Why did you not seek advancement in office, causing our meeting to be late?"
translations.idiomatic: "Taizu asked, "Why did you not seek office, so that we meet only so late?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣草野蠢愚，無以裨聖化。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject is a crude, foolish man of the wilds and has nothing with which to assist sagely transformation.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I am but a crude rustic, Your Majesty, and have nothing to offer your sage rule.

sentences.zh: 」賜坐，令講《易·乾卦》，召宰相薛居正等觀之，至「飛龍在天」，上曰：「此書豈可令常人見？

translations.literal: " He was granted a seat and ordered to lecture on the Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes; the chief minister Xue Juzheng and others were summoned to observe. When they reached "flying dragon in heaven," the emperor said, "Can this book really be shown to ordinary men?
translations.idiomatic: He was given a seat and asked to expound the Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes; the chief minister Xue Juzheng and others were called in to listen. At the line "The flying dragon is in heaven," the emperor said, "Surely this book is not for ordinary eyes?

sentences.zh: 」昭素對曰：「此書非聖人出不能合其象。

translations.literal: " Zhaosu replied: "This book—unless a sage appears, one cannot match its images.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosu answered, "Only when a sage appears can anyone truly grasp these images.

sentences.zh: 」因訪以民間事，昭素所言誠實無隱，上嘉之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he inquired about matters among the people; what Zhaosu said was honest and without concealment, and the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked him about conditions among the people. Zhaosu spoke frankly and held nothing back, and the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 以衰老求歸鄉里，拜國子博士致仕，賜茶藥及錢二十萬，留月餘，遣之。

translations.literal: Citing old age, he asked to return to his native place; he was appointed Doctor at the Imperial University and retired, was granted tea and medicines plus two hundred thousand in cash, was kept over a month, and then sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Pleading age, he asked to go home. He was made a university doctor and retired, given tea, medicines, and two hundred thousand cash. After more than a month he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 年八十九，卒於家。

translations.literal: At age eighty-nine he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 昭素頗有人倫鑒。

translations.literal: Zhaosu had considerable insight into human character.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosu had a keen eye for men.

sentences.zh: 初，李穆兄弟從昭素學《易》，常謂穆曰：「子所謂精理，往往出吾意表。

translations.literal: Early on, the Li Mu brothers studied the Changes under Zhaosu; he often told Mu: "The refined principles you speak of often go beyond my expectations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Li Mu brothers studied the Changes with him, he often told Mu, "Your subtle points often go beyond what I had in mind.

sentences.zh: 」又語人曰：「穆兄弟皆令器，穆尤沈厚，他日必至廊廟。

translations.literal: " He also told people: "The Mu brothers are all fine vessels; Mu especially is deep and steady—in time he will surely reach the halls of state.
translations.idiomatic: He also said of them, "The Mu brothers are all men of promise; Mu above all is grave and steady—one day he will sit in the highest councils.

sentences.zh: 」後果參知政事。

translations.literal: " Later he indeed became Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Mu later did become vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 昭素每市物，隨所言而還直，未嘗論高下。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhaosu bought goods he paid whatever price was named and never haggled over high or low.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaosu bought anything, he paid whatever was asked and never bargained.

sentences.zh: 縣人相告曰：「王先生市物，無得高取其價也。

translations.literal: The people of the county told one another: "When Mr. Wang buys goods, do not take an inflated price.
translations.idiomatic: People in the county warned one another: "When Mr. Wang comes to market, do not overcharge him.

sentences.zh: 」治所居室，有椽木積門中，夜有盜者抉門將入，昭素覺之，即自門中潛擲椽於外，盜者慚而去，由是里中無盜。

translations.literal: " While repairing his dwelling he piled rafter wood in the doorway. At night a thief pried the door intending to enter; Zhaosu noticed and quietly threw rafters out from inside the door. The thief departed in shame, and thereafter the neighborhood had no thieves.
translations.idiomatic: While repairing his house he stacked rafters in the doorway. One night a thief pried the door open; Zhaosu heard him and quietly tossed rafters out into the yard. The thief slunk away in shame, and after that the lane had no more thieves.

sentences.zh: 家有一驢，人多來假，將出，先問僮奴曰：「外無假驢者乎？

translations.literal: His household had one donkey and many people came to borrow it; before going out he would first ask his servants: "Is anyone outside waiting to borrow the donkey?
translations.idiomatic: The family owned a single donkey, and neighbors often borrowed it. Before he went out himself, he would ask his servants, "Is anyone waiting outside to borrow the donkey?

sentences.zh: 」對云「無」，然後出。

translations.literal: " They would answer "No," and only then would he go out.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they answered "No" would he leave.

sentences.zh: 其為純質若此。

translations.literal: Such was his simple, upright character.
translations.idiomatic: That was the sort of plain, honest man he was.

sentences.zh: 子仁著，亦有隱德。

translations.literal: His son Renzhe also possessed hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renzhe likewise lived by quiet virtue.

sentences.zh: 孔維，字為則，開封雍丘人。

translations.literal: Kong Wei, courtesy name Weize, was a man of Yongqiu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei, styled Weize, was from Yongqiu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年《九經》及第，解褐東明、鄢陵二主簿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande he passed the Nine Classics examination, doffed his commoner's garb, and served as registrar in both Dongming and Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 4 he passed the Nine Classics examination, entered office, and served as registrar in Dongming and Yanling.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，禮部再奏為考試官，調滁州軍事推官。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao period the Ministry of Rites again recommended him as an examiner; he was transferred to military reviewing officer in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao the Ministry of Rites again nominated him as an examiner, and he was posted as military reviewing officer in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，擢授太子左讚善大夫、知河南縣，通判滑、梓二州。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, he was promoted and appointed Left Tutor to the Heir Apparent and magistrate of Henan County, and served as vice-prefect in both Hua and Zi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Wei was promoted to left tutor of the heir apparent and magistrate of Henan County, and served as vice-prefect of Hua and Zi.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，就拜國子《周易》博士，代還，遷《禮記》博士。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo period he was appointed on the spot as Doctor of the Book of Changes at the Imperial University; when his replacement arrived he was transferred to Doctor of the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo he was appointed university lecturer on the Book of Changes on the spot; when his tour ended he became lecturer on the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 七年，使高麗，王治問禮於維，維對以君父臣子之道，升降等威之序，治悅，稱之曰：「今日復見中國之夫子也。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was envoy to Goryeo. King Zhi asked Wei about ritual; Wei replied concerning the Way of ruler and father, minister and son, and the order of rising, descending, and ranks of dignity. Zhi was pleased and said of him: "Today I have again seen a Master of China.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he went as envoy to Goryeo. King Zhi questioned him on ritual, and Wei answered with the relations of ruler and subject, father and son, and the proper order of precedence. Delighted, the king said, "Today I have met a true master of China again.

sentences.zh: 」九年，判國學事。

translations.literal: " In the ninth year he was assigned to oversee Imperial University affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was put in charge of university affairs.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，遷主客員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was promoted to Vice Director in the Host Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongxi he was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of Hosts and Guests.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢為國子司業，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the third year he was elevated to Vice-Director of the Imperial University and granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made vice-director of the imperial university and given the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 會將有事於籍田，維起《周禮》至於《唐書》，凡沿革制度並錄之以獻，觀者稱其博。

translations.literal: When the plowing ceremony at the sacred field was to be held, Wei compiled from the Rites of Zhou through the Tang History all institutions and their changes and submitted them; observers praised his breadth of learning.
translations.idiomatic: When a sacred-field plowing rite was planned, Wei gathered every relevant institution and its evolution from the Rites of Zhou through the Tang History and presented the compilation; readers marveled at his erudition.

sentences.zh: 又上書請禁原蠶以利國馬。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial requesting prohibition of late silkworms to benefit the state horses.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized asking that late-season silkworm rearing be banned to protect the state's horses.

sentences.zh: 直史館樂史駁之曰：

translations.literal: Le Shi of the Historiography Institute rebutted him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Le Shi, a compiler at the Historiography Institute, objected:

sentences.zh: 《管子》云：「倉稟實，知禮節；

translations.literal: The Guanzi says: "When the granaries are full, the people know ritual and propriety;
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzi says, "When granaries are full, the people know ritual and propriety;

sentences.zh: 衣食足，知榮辱。

translations.literal: when clothing and food are sufficient, they know honor and shame.
translations.idiomatic: when clothing and food are enough, they know honor and shame.

sentences.zh: 」是以古先哲王厚農桑之業，以其為衣食之原耳。

translations.literal: " Therefore the ancient sage kings enriched farming and sericulture because these are the sources of clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: " That is why the ancient sage kings prized farming and sericulture: they are the root of food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 一夫不耕，天下有受其饑者；

translations.literal: If one man does not plow, someone in the realm will go hungry;
translations.idiomatic: If one man does not plow, someone under Heaven will hunger;

sentences.zh: 一婦不蠶，天下有受其寒者。

translations.literal: if one woman does not raise silkworms, someone in the realm will suffer cold.
translations.idiomatic: if one woman does not raise silkworms, someone under Heaven will freeze.

sentences.zh: 故天子親耕，后妃親蠶，屈身以化下者，邦國之重務也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Son of Heaven plows in person and the empress raises silkworms in person—stooping the body to transform those below is a weighty task of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Son of Heaven plows in person and the empress feeds silkworms in person: by humbling themselves to teach the people, they fulfill one of the state's gravest duties.

sentences.zh: 《吳都賦》曰：「國賦再熟之稻，鄉貢八蠶之綿。

translations.literal: The Rhapsody on the Wu Capital says: "The state levies double-harvest rice; the districts present silk from eight broods of silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: The Rhapsody on the Wu Capital says, "The state levies double-cropped rice; the districts send up silk from eight broods of worms.

sentences.zh: 」則蠶之有原，其來舊矣。

translations.literal: " Thus the practice of late silkworms is of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: " Late silkworm rearing, then, is no new custom.

sentences.zh: 今孔維請禁原蠶以利國馬，徒引前經物類同氣之文，不究時事確實之理。

translations.literal: Now Kong Wei asks to prohibit late silkworms to benefit state horses, merely citing passages from earlier classics about things of the same qi, without investigating what present circumstances truly require.
translations.idiomatic: Now Kong Wei would ban late silkworms for the sake of the state's horses, citing old texts about creatures sharing the same vital force while ignoring what the times actually demand.

sentences.zh: 夫所市國馬來自外方，涉遠馳驅，虧其秣飼，失於善視，遂至玄黃，致斃之由，鮮不以此。

translations.literal: The state horses that are purchased come from abroad; driven far and hard, their fodder is stinted and their care neglected, until they sicken and die—the reason they perish is almost always this.
translations.idiomatic: The horses the state buys come from distant regions; after long travel and hard riding they are underfed and poorly tended, until they fail and die—and that, not silkworms, is why they die.

sentences.zh: 今乃欲禁其蠶事，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: Now to wish to ban sericulture is utterly pointless.
translations.idiomatic: To ban sericulture on such grounds is absurd.

sentences.zh: 唐朝畜馬，具存監牧之制，詳觀本書，亦無禁蠶之文。

translations.literal: The Tang dynasty raised horses and fully maintained the system of supervisory pastures; reading that book in detail, there is likewise no text forbidding silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang kept horses under a full system of pasture supervision; read the histories carefully and you will find no ban on silkworms there either.

sentences.zh: 況近降明詔，來年春有事於籍田，是則勸農之典方行，而禁蠶之制又下，事相違戾，恐非所長。

translations.literal: Moreover, a bright edict has lately been issued that next spring there will be a plowing ceremony at the sacred field—thus the rite encouraging agriculture is just about to be carried out, while a prohibition on silkworms is also issued; the two policies contradict each other and can hardly be called wise.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the court has just proclaimed a sacred-field plowing for next spring even as it would forbid late silkworms—the one exhorts the people to farm, the other forbids them to raise silk. The policies clash, and that is no way to govern.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗曆職州縣，粗知利病，編民之內，貧窶者多，春蠶所成，止充賦調之備，晚蠶薄利，始及卒歲之資。

translations.literal: Your subject has served in prefectures and counties and has a rough knowledge of benefits and harms; among the registered populace the poor are many. What the spring silkworms yield barely covers taxes and levies; only the small profit of late silkworms supplies what is needed to last out the year.
translations.idiomatic: I have served in the provinces and know something of local hardship. Among common people the poor are many: the spring crop of silk barely pays taxes and corvée; only the slender profit of a late brood gets a household through the year.

sentences.zh: 今若禁其後圖，必有因緣為弊，滋彰撓亂，民豈皇寧。

translations.literal: If the late crop is now forbidden, people will surely find pretexts for abuse, confusion will spread, and how can the people live in peace?
translations.idiomatic: Ban the late brood and people will invent evasions; disorder will spread, and the common folk will know no rest.

sentences.zh: 渙汗絲綸，所宜重慎。

translations.literal: Imperial edicts flowing forth like sweat from every pore should be issued with the greatest caution.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial words are not to be issued lightly.

sentences.zh: 上覽之，遂寢晚蠶之禁。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and thereupon shelved the prohibition on late silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and dropped the proposed ban.

sentences.zh: 維復抗疏曰：

translations.literal: Wei submitted another forthright memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wei submitted another forceful memorial:

sentences.zh: 按《周禮·夏官·司馬》職禁原蠶者，為傷馬也。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, Summer Office, Grand Marshal, the duty of forbidding late silkworms exists because they harm horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, in the Grand Marshal's duties, forbids late silkworms because they injure horses.

sentences.zh: 原，再也。

translations.literal: Yuan means "again."
translations.idiomatic: "Yuan" means a second brood.

sentences.zh: 天文，辰為馬。

translations.literal: In astronomy, the chen asterism corresponds to the horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the heavens, the chen mansion belongs to the horse.

sentences.zh: 《蠶書》，蠶為龍精，月直大火，則浴其種。

translations.literal: The Book of Silkworms says that the silkworm is the essence of the dragon; when the moon stands in the Great Fire, the eggs are bathed.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Silkworms says the worm is dragon-spirit; when the moon enters the Great Fire asterism, the eggs are washed.

sentences.zh: 是蠶與馬同氣，物莫能兩大，故禁再蠶以益馬也。

translations.literal: Thus silkworm and horse share the same qi; two things cannot both grow great, and therefore late silkworms are forbidden to benefit horses.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworm and horse share one vital force; two powers cannot both flourish, so a second brood is forbidden to strengthen the horse.

sentences.zh: 又郭璞云：「重蠶為原，今晚蠶也。

translations.literal: Guo Pu also says: "A repeated brood is yuan—today's late silkworm.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu likewise says, "A repeated brood is yuan—that is, the late silkworm.

sentences.zh: 」臣少親耕桑之務，長曆州縣之職，物之利害，盡知之矣。

translations.literal: " Your subject in youth personally engaged in farming and sericulture and in adulthood served in prefectures and counties; he knows thoroughly what helps and what harms.
translations.idiomatic: " I farmed and raised silkworms as a youth and later governed counties and prefectures; I know exactly where the gain and the harm lie.

sentences.zh: 蚩蚩之氓知其利而不知其害，故有早蠶之後，重養晚蠶之繭，出絲甚少，再采之葉來歲不茂，豈止傷及於馬，而桑亦損矣。

translations.literal: The common folk know the profit but not the harm; therefore after the early silkworms they raise a late brood, yet the cocoons yield very little silk, and leaves picked a second time will not flourish the next year—this harms not only horses but mulberry trees as well.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary people see the profit, not the damage: after the spring brood they raise a late one, but the cocoons yield little silk, and leaves stripped twice leave the mulberry weak the next year. The harm is not to horses alone—the trees suffer too.

sentences.zh: 臣自縣曆官，路見野之地官馬多死，若非明援典據，助其畜牧，安敢妄有舉陳哉。

translations.literal: Since your subject rose from county office, on the road he has seen in open country many official horses dead; if he did not have clear canonical authority to support horse-rearing, how would he dare make this proposal rashly?
translations.idiomatic: Since I began in county office I have traveled the roads and seen many government horses dead in the wild. Without clear classical grounds for aiding the herds, I would not have dared speak.

sentences.zh: 按《本草》注：「以僵蠶塗馬齒，則不能食草。

translations.literal: According to a note in the Materia Medica: "If stiff silkworms are smeared on a horse's teeth, it cannot eat grass.
translations.idiomatic: A note in the Materia Medica says, "Rub a horse's teeth with stiff silkworms and it will not eat grass.

sentences.zh: 」物類相感如此。

translations.literal: " Things of the same kind affect one another thus.
translations.idiomatic: " Creatures of a kind react on one another in just this way.

sentences.zh: 《月令》仲春祭馬祖，季春享先蠶，皆謂天駟房星也，為馬祈福，謂之馬祖，為蠶祈福，謂之先蠶，是蠶與馬同其類爾。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances: in mid-spring sacrifice is made to the Horse Ancestor; in late spring the Silkworm Ancestor is honored—both refer to the Heavenly Team in the Room mansion. Blessings for the horse are called the Horse Ancestor; blessings for the silkworm are called the Silkworm Ancestor—thus silkworm and horse belong to the same category.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances sacrifice to the Horse Ancestor in mid-spring and to the Silkworm Ancestor in late spring—both rites address the Heavenly Team in the Room star. One rite blesses the horse, the other the silkworm; silkworm and horse are of one kind.

sentences.zh: 蠶重則馬損，氣感之而然也。

translations.literal: When silkworms are doubled, horses are harmed—it is because their qi interact thus.
translations.idiomatic: When the silkworm brood is doubled, horses decline—such is the working of shared vital force.

sentences.zh: 臣謂依《周禮》禁原蠶為當。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that forbidding late silkworms according to the Rites of Zhou is correct.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the Zhou rite forbidding a second brood should stand.

sentences.zh: 上雖不用維言，而嘉其援引經據，以章付史館。

translations.literal: Although the emperor did not adopt Wei's words, he commended his citation of classical authority and had the memorial sent to the Historiography Institute for record.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not follow Wei's advice, but praised his use of the classics and had the memorial filed at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 籍田畢，拜國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When the sacred-field rite was completed, he was appointed Rector of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: After the plowing ceremony he was made rector of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，兼工部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he also served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chunhua he also held the post of vice director of works.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the second year he died at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 維通經術。

translations.literal: Wei was thoroughly versed in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had mastered the classical tradition.

sentences.zh: 準舊制，舉《九經》，一上不中第即改科。

translations.literal: Under the old system, in the Nine Classics examination, if one failed on the first attempt one had to change fields.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, candidates in the Nine Classics who failed once had to switch to another subject.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，維論其事非便，詔禮部自今《九經》同諸科許再赴舉。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao period Wei argued that this was inconvenient; an edict ordered that from then on candidates in the Nine Classics, like those in other subjects, might sit the examination a second time.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao, Wei argued that this was unfair, and the throne ordered that Nine Classics candidates, like others, be allowed a second attempt.

sentences.zh: 嘗建議乞廣太學，上以侵壞民舍不許。

translations.literal: He once proposed expanding the Imperial University; the emperor did not permit it because it would encroach on private dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: He once asked to enlarge the imperial university, but the emperor refused lest it destroy private homes.

sentences.zh: 受詔與學官校定《五經疏義》，刻板行用，功未及畢，被病，上遣太醫診視，使者撫問。

translations.literal: He received an edict to join the academic officials in collating the Exegeses of the Five Classics, carving blocks for circulation; the work was not yet finished when he fell ill; the emperor sent the imperial physician to examine him and dispatched envoys to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to join the academicians in editing the Five Classics commentaries for block printing, he fell ill before the work was done; the emperor sent his physician and messengers to visit him.

sentences.zh: 初，維私用印書錢三十餘萬，為掌事黃門所發，維憂懼，遽以家財賞之，疾遂亟，上赦而不問。

translations.literal: Early on, Wei had privately used more than three hundred thousand in printing funds; the eunuch in charge exposed this. Wei, fearful, hastily compensated the sum from his family wealth; his illness then grew acute. The emperor pardoned him and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had diverted more than three hundred thousand cash of printing funds; the supervising eunuch reported it. In terror Wei repaid the sum from his estate, his illness worsened sharply, and the emperor pardoned him without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 維將終，召其婿鄭革口授遺表，以《五經疏》未畢為恨。

translations.literal: As Wei was dying he summoned his son-in-law Zheng Ge and dictated a final memorial, regretting that the Five Classics exegeses were not complete.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he called his son-in-law Zheng Ge and dictated a final memorial, grieving that the Five Classics commentary remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，錄其孫禹圭同學究出身。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde his grandson Yugui was enrolled with the rank of fellow classicist.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 4 his grandson Yugui was granted entry as a fellow classicist.

sentences.zh: 孔宜，字不疑，兗州曲阜人，孔子四十四世孫。

translations.literal: Kong Yi, courtesy name Buyi, was a man of Qufu in Yanzhou, forty-fourth-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yi, styled Buyi, was from Qufu in Yanzhou, a forty-fourth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 孔子生鯉，字伯魚。

translations.literal: Confucius begat Li, courtesy name Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius had a son Li, styled Boyu.

sentences.zh: 鯉生伋，字子思。

translations.literal: Li begat Ji, courtesy name Zisi.
translations.idiomatic: Li had a son Ji, styled Zisi.

sentences.zh: 伋生白，字子上。

translations.literal: Ji begat Bai, courtesy name Zishang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had a son Bai, styled Zishang.

sentences.zh: 白生求，字子家。

translations.literal: Bai begat Qiu, courtesy name Zijia.
translations.idiomatic: Bai had a son Qiu, styled Zijia.

sentences.zh: 求生箕，字子京。

translations.literal: Qiu begat Ji, courtesy name Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had a son Ji, styled Zijing.

sentences.zh: 箕生穿，字子高。

translations.literal: Ji begat Chuan, courtesy name Zigao.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had a son Chuan, styled Zigao.

sentences.zh: 穿生謙，字子慎。

translations.literal: Chuan begat Qian, courtesy name Zishen.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan had a son Qian, styled Zishen.

sentences.zh: 謙生鮒，字子魚，以弟子騰為嗣。

translations.literal: Qian begat Fu, courtesy name Ziyu; he took his younger brother's son Teng as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had a son Fu, styled Ziyu, who adopted his younger brother's son Teng as heir.

sentences.zh: 騰字子襄，值秦難，藏其家書於屋壁。

translations.literal: Teng, courtesy name Zixiang, at the crisis of Qin hid his family books in the wall of the house.
translations.idiomatic: Teng, styled Zixiang, at the fall of Qin hid the family classics in a wall of the house.

sentences.zh: 騰生正，字季忠。

translations.literal: Teng begat Zheng, courtesy name Jizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Teng had a son Zheng, styled Jizhong.

sentences.zh: 忠生武。

translations.literal: Zhong begat Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had a son Wu.

sentences.zh: 武生延年及安國。

translations.literal: Wu begat Yan Nian and An Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had sons Yan Nian and An Guo.

sentences.zh: 延年生霸，字次孺，漢昭帝時為博士，宣帝時為太中大夫，授皇太子經。

translations.literal: Yan Nian begat Ba, courtesy name Ciru; under Emperor Zhao of Han he was a doctor; under Emperor Xuan he was Grand Master of Palace Counsel and instructed the crown prince in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Nian had a son Ba, styled Ciru, who served as a classicist under Emperor Zhao of Han and as grand master of palace counsel under Emperor Xuan, instructing the crown prince in the classics.

sentences.zh: 元帝即位，賜爵關內侯，號褒成君。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan acceded he was granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes and was titled Lord Baocheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan took the throne, Ba was made marquis within the passes with the title Lord Baocheng.

sentences.zh: 霸生福。

translations.literal: Ba begat Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Ba had a son Fu.

sentences.zh: 福生房。

translations.literal: Fu begat Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had a son Fang.

sentences.zh: 房生均，字長平，好學有才，為尚書郎，平帝元始元年，封均為褒成侯，食邑二千戶，追諡夫子為褒成宣尼公。

translations.literal: Fang begat Jun, courtesy name Changping, who loved learning and had talent; he was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; in the first year of Yuanshi of Emperor Ping he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Baocheng with a fief of two thousand households, and the Master was posthumously titled Lord Baocheng, Sage Ni.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had a son Jun, styled Changping, a gifted scholar and gentleman of the masters of writing; in Yuanshi 1 of Emperor Ping, Jun was enfeoffed as Marquis of Baocheng with two thousand households, and Confucius was posthumously titled Lord Baocheng, Sage Ni.

sentences.zh: 王莽以均為太尉，三以疾辭，得還，莽敗，失國。

translations.literal: Wang Mang made Jun Grand Commandant; three times he declined citing illness and was permitted to return; when Mang fell he lost the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang appointed Jun grand commandant; three times Jun declined on grounds of illness and was allowed to retire; when Mang fell, the fief was lost.

sentences.zh: 後漢世祖建武十四年，復封均子誌為褒成侯，諡元成。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jianwu of the Later Han Founder, Jun's son Zhi was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Baocheng with the posthumous title Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han Jianwu 14, Jun's son Zhi was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Baocheng with the posthumous title Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 誌生損，襲爵，和帝永元四年，徙封損為褒亭侯。

translations.literal: Zhi begat Sun, who inherited the title; in the fourth year of Yongyuan of Emperor He, Sun was moved to Marquis of Baoting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had a son Sun, who inherited the title; in Yongyuan 4 of Emperor He, Sun was transferred to Marquis of Baoting.

sentences.zh: 損卒，子曜嗣侯、邑千戶。

translations.literal: Sun died; his son Yao succeeded as marquis with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Sun died; his son Yao succeeded as marquis with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 子完嗣，邑百戶。

translations.literal: His son Wan succeeded with a fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's son Wan succeeded with a fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 完早卒無子，以弟子羨襲爵。

translations.literal: Wan died early without a son; his younger brother's son Xian succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: Wan died young without heirs; his nephew Xian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 渠生長孫，隋文帝復封長孫為鄒國公。

translations.literal: Qu begat Changsun; Emperor Wen of Sui again enfeoffed Changsun as Duke of Zou.
translations.idiomatic: Qu had a son Changsun; Emperor Wen of Sui again enfeoffed Changsun as Duke of Zou.

sentences.zh: 長孫生嗣哲，應製舉，曆涇州司兵參軍、太子通事舍人，大業四年，改封紹聖侯、邑百戶。

translations.literal: Changsun begat Sizhe, who entered the imperial examination, served as military adjutant of Jing Prefecture and Supervisor of Affairs for the Heir Apparent; in the fourth year of Daye he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Shaosheng with a fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun had a son Sizhe, who took the imperial examination, served as military adjutant of Jing Prefecture and supervisor of affairs for the heir apparent, and in Daye 4 was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Shaosheng with a fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 嗣哲生德倫，唐太宗貞觀十一年，封褒聖侯，邑百戶，朝會位同三品，復其子孫。

translations.literal: Sizhe begat Delun; in the eleventh year of Zhenguan of Tang Taizong he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Baosheng with a fief of one hundred households, court precedence equal to third rank, and his descendants were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhe had a son Delun; in Tang Zhenguan 11, Taizong enfeoffed him as Marquis of Baosheng with a fief of one hundred households, court rank equal to third grade, and restored the line.

sentences.zh: 則天天授二年，賜德倫璽書、衣服。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou of Empress Zetian, Delun was granted an imperial seal-letter and robes.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu Zetian's Tianshou 2, Delun received an imperial edict under seal and formal robes as gifts.

sentences.zh: 德化生崇基，襲侯，中宗神龍元年，授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Delun begat Chongji, who inherited the marquisate; in the first year of Shentong of Zhongzong he was appointed Grand Master of Dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: Delun's son Chongji inherited the title; in Shenlong 1 of Emperor Zhongzong he was made Grand Master of Dispersal.

sentences.zh: 崇基生遂之，玄宗開元中，曆國子四門博士、邠王府文學、蔡州長史。

translations.literal: Chongji begat Suizhi; in the Kaiyuan era of Xuanzong he successively served as Doctor of the Four Gates at the Directorate of Education, Literary Attendant of the Prince of Bin's household, and Chief Administrator of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji had a son Suizhi who, during Xuanzong's Kaiyuan reign, served as a Four Gates doctor at the Imperial University, literary attendant to the Prince of Bin, and chief administrator of Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，詔追諡孔子為文宣王，改封褒聖侯禘之為襲文宣公，兼兗州長史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, an edict posthumously ennobled Confucius as King Wenxuan, changed the enfeoffment of Marquis of Baosheng Di Zhi to Heir Duke Wenxuan, and concurrently appointed him Chief Administrator of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27, an edict posthumously honored Confucius as King Wenxuan, re-enfeoffed Marquis of Baosheng Di Zhi as Duke Wenxuan in succession, and made him concurrently chief administrator of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遂之生萱，襲封，曆兗州泗水令。

translations.literal: Suizhi begat Xuan, who inherited the enfeoffment and served as Magistrate of Sishui in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Suizhi's son Xuan inherited the title and served as magistrate of Sishui in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 萱生齊卿，德宗建中三年，詔以齊卿為兗州司馬，陷於東平，卒。

translations.literal: Xuan begat Qingqing; in the third year of Jianzhong of Dezong an edict appointed Qingqing as Deputy Military Governor of Yan Prefecture; he was trapped at Dongping and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had a son Qingqing; in Jianzhong 3 of Dezong an edict made him deputy military governor of Yan Prefecture. He was trapped at Dongping and died.

sentences.zh: 至憲宗元和十三年，平李師道，其子惟至歸魯，詔以惟至為兗州參軍，奉夫子祀，復五十戶，以供灑掃。

translations.literal: By the thirteenth year of Yuanhe of Xianzong, when Li Shidao was pacified, his son Weizhi returned to Lu; an edict appointed Weizhi as Military Aide of Yan Prefecture to attend to the worship of the Master, restored fifty households to supply sweeping and cleaning.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianzong's Yuanhe 13, after Li Shidao was defeated, Qingqing's son Weizhi returned to Lu. An edict appointed Weizhi military aide of Yan Prefecture to maintain the Master's rites, restoring fifty households for temple upkeep.

sentences.zh: 惟至生策，會昌元年，曆國子監丞、尚書博士。

translations.literal: Weizhi begat Ce; in the first year of Huichang he successively served as Assistant Director of the Directorate of Education and Doctor of the Book of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi's son Ce, in Huichang 1, served as assistant director of the Imperial University and doctor of the Book of Documents.

sentences.zh: 大中元年，宰相白敏中奏歲給封戶絹百匹，充春秋奉祀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong, Chief Minister Bai Minzhong memorialized that yearly a hundred bolts of silk from enfeoffed households be granted for spring and autumn offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 1, Chancellor Bai Minzhong petitioned for an annual grant of a hundred bolts of silk from the fief households for the spring and autumn ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 自遂之至策，五世並襲封文宣公。

translations.literal: From Suizhi to Ce, five generations all inherited the enfeoffment as Duke Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: From Suizhi through Ce, five generations in succession held the title Duke Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 策生振，懿宗咸通四年，舉進士甲科，曆兗州觀察判官，至刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Ce begat Zhen; in the fourth year of Xiantong of Yizong he passed the jinshi examination in the top tier, served as aide to the military commissioner of Yan Prefecture, and rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Ce had a son Zhen who, in Xiantong 4 of Yizong, passed the jinshi in the highest grade, served as staff officer to the Yanzhou observation commissioner, and reached vice director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 振生昭儉，曆袞州司馬、曲阜令。

translations.literal: Zhen begat Zhaolian, who served as Deputy Military Governor of Yan Prefecture and Magistrate of Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's son Zhaolian served as deputy military governor of Yan Prefecture and magistrate of Qufu.

sentences.zh: 自策至昭儉，三世歲給封絹，以供享祀。

translations.literal: From Ce to Zhaolian, three generations annually received enfeoffed silk for offerings.
translations.idiomatic: From Ce through Zhaolian, three generations received annual silk from the fief for sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 昭儉生光嗣，哀帝天祐中，為泗水主簿，奉孔子祀。

translations.literal: Zhaolian begat Guangsi; during the Tianyou era of Emperor Ai he was Registrar of Sishui, attending to Confucius worship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolian's son Guangsi, in the Tianyou years of Emperor Ai, served as registrar of Sishui and maintained the Confucian rites.

sentences.zh: 仁玉四子，長曰宜，舉進士不第，乾德中詣闕上書，述其家世，詔以為曲阜主簿，曆黃州軍事推官，遷司農寺丞，掌星子鎮市征。

translations.literal: Renyu had four sons; the eldest was Yi, who failed the jinshi examination; in the Qiande era he went to court with a written submission describing his family lineage, and an edict appointed him Registrar of Qufu; he served as military investigating officer of Huang Prefecture, was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, and managed market taxes at Xingzi garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Renyu had four sons. The eldest, Yi, failed the jinshi examination; in the Qiande era he went to court with a memorial on his family lineage and was appointed registrar of Qufu. He served as military investigating officer of Huang Prefecture, rose to vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture, and managed market taxes at Xingzi garrison.

sentences.zh: 宜上言：「星子當江湖之會，商賈所集，請建為軍。

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial: "Xingzi lies at the junction of rivers and lakes, a gathering place for merchants; I request that it be established as a military garrison."
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial: "Xingzi sits where rivers and lakes meet and merchants gather; I ask that it be made a military garrison."

sentences.zh: 」詔以為縣，就命宜知縣事，後以為南康軍。

translations.literal: An edict established it as a county, and Yi was immediately ordered to administer county affairs; later it became Nankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made it a county and immediately put Yi in charge of its affairs; later it was elevated to Nankang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 宜代還，獻文賦數十篇，太宗覽而嘉之，召見，問以孔子世嗣，因下詔曰：「素王之道，百代所崇，傳祚襲封，抑存典制。

translations.literal: When Yi's term ended and he returned, he presented several dozen literary rhapsodies; Taizong read them with approval, summoned him for audience, and questioned him about the hereditary succession of Confucius; thereby an edict was issued: "The way of the Uncrowned King has been honored for a hundred generations; transmitting the fief and inheriting the seal yet preserves the canonical institution."
translations.idiomatic: When Yi's term ended and he returned, he presented dozens of literary rhapsodies. Taizong read them with approval, summoned him, and questioned him about the Confucian line of succession. An edict followed: "The way of the Uncrowned King has been revered for a hundred generations; passing down the fief and inheriting the title preserves the ancient institution."

sentences.zh: 文宣王四十四代孫、司農寺丞宜服勤素業，砥礪廉隅，亟曆官聯，洽聞政績，聖人之後，世德不衰，俾登朝倫，以光儒胄。

translations.literal: Forty-fourth-generation descendant of King Wenxuan, Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Yi, diligent in his hereditary calling, sharpening his moral integrity, having swiftly passed through official posts with well-known administrative achievements—descendant of the Sage, whose family virtue does not decline—shall be advanced among court ranks to glorify the Confucian line.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, forty-fourth-generation descendant of King Wenxuan and vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture, has been diligent in his hereditary calling, cultivated his integrity, moved swiftly through office with a reputation for achievement, and, as a sage's descendant whose family virtue has not faded, shall be raised among court ranks to honor the Confucian line.

sentences.zh: 可太子右讚善大夫，襲封文宣公，復其家。

translations.literal: He is approved as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace, to inherit Duke Wenxuan, restoring his family.
