translations.literal: , adding a slanting stroke or a dot above yong neither forms a character."
translations.idiomatic: , adding a slanting stroke or a dot above yong neither forms a character."

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，真宗幸國學，召偓佺說《尚書》，即特賜緋。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, Emperor Zhenzong visited the National University, summoned Woquan to expound the Book of Documents, and immediately specially granted him purple.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2, Emperor Zhenzong visited the National University, summoned Woquan to expound the Book of Documents, and immediately specially granted him purple robes.

sentences.zh: 景德後，令講《道德經》，日於崇文院候對。

translations.literal: After Jingde, he was ordered to expound the Classic of the Way and Its Power, daily awaiting audience at the Chongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingde, he was ordered to expound the Classic of the Way and Its Power, daily awaiting audience at the Chongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 終篇，賜以白金繒彩。

translations.literal: When the text was finished, he was granted white gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: When the text was finished, he was granted white gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jingde 3, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 嘗撰《帝王手鑒》十卷，並注曹唐《大遊仙詩》十五卷。

translations.literal: He once compiled the Imperial Mirror in Ten Scrolls and also annotated Cao Tang's Great Wandering Immortal Poems in Fifteen Scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled the Imperial Mirror in Ten Scrolls and also annotated Cao Tang's Great Wandering Immortal Poems in Fifteen Scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其子世安上之，特賜出身。

translations.literal: His son Shi'an presented them to the throne and was specially granted initial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi'an presented them to the throne and was specially granted initial appointment.

sentences.zh: 李之才

translations.literal: Li Zhicai
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhicai

sentences.zh: 李之才字挺之，青社人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhicai, styled Tingzhi, was a man of Qing She.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhicai, styled Tingzhi, was from Qing She.

sentences.zh: 天聖八年同進士出身，為人樸且率，自信，無少矯厲。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiansheng he passed the jinshi examination and began his career; as a man he was plain and straightforward, self-assured, without the least affectation.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiansheng 8 he passed the jinshi examination and began his career. Plain and straightforward by nature, he was self-assured and wholly without affectation.

sentences.zh: 師河南穆修，修性莊嚴寡合，雖之才亦頻在訶怒中，之才事之益謹，卒能受《易》。

translations.literal: He studied under Mu Xiu of Henan; Xiu was stern and aloof by nature, and even Zhicai often found himself amid scolding and anger, yet Zhicai served him all the more carefully and in the end was able to receive the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Mu Xiu of Henan. Xiu was stern and aloof by nature, and even Zhicai often found himself amid scolding and anger, yet Zhicai served him all the more carefully and in the end received the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 時蘇舜欽輩亦從修學《易》，其專授受者惟之才爾。

translations.literal: At that time Su Shunqin and others also studied the Book of Changes under Xiu, but the one who received his full personal transmission was only Zhicai.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Su Shunqin and others also studied the Book of Changes under Xiu, but the one who received his full personal transmission was Zhicai alone.

sentences.zh: 脩之《易》受之種放，放受之陳摶，源流最遠，其圖書象數變通之妙，秦、漢以來鮮有知者。

translations.literal: Xiu's Book of Changes was received from Zhong Fang, and Fang's from Chen Tuan; the lineage was most remote, and the subtlety of its diagrams, writings, numerology, and transformations—since Qin and Han there have been few who understood it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's Book of Changes came from Zhong Fang, and Fang's from Chen Tuan; the lineage was most remote, and the subtlety of its diagrams, writings, numerology, and transformations had been understood by few since Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 之才初為衛州獲嘉主簿、權共城令。

translations.literal: Zhicai first served as registrar of Huojia in Wei Prefecture and acting magistrate of Gongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai first served as registrar of Huojia in Wei Prefecture and acting magistrate of Gongcheng.

sentences.zh: 時邵雍居母憂於蘇門山百源之上，布裘蔬食，躬爨以養父。

translations.literal: At that time Shao Yong was in mourning for his mother on the Hundred Springs above Mount Sumen, wearing cloth robes and eating vegetables, personally cooking to support his father.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shao Yong was in mourning for his mother on the Hundred Springs above Mount Sumen, wearing cloth robes and eating vegetables and personally cooking to support his father.

sentences.zh: 之才叩門來謁，勞苦之曰：「好學篤誌果何似？

translations.literal: Zhicai knocked at the door and came to call on him, expressing sympathy and saying: "What is your earnest love of learning and firm resolve really like?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai knocked at the door and came to call on him, expressing sympathy and saying: "What is your earnest love of learning and firm resolve really like?"

sentences.zh: 」雍曰：「簡策之外，未有跡也。

translations.literal: Yong said: "Beyond bamboo slips and written records, there is no trace yet."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said: "Beyond bamboo slips and written records, there is no trace yet."

sentences.zh: 」之才曰：「君非跡簡策者，其如物理之學何？

translations.literal: Zhicai said: "You are not one who leaves traces only in written records—what about the study of natural principle?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said: "You are not one who leaves traces only in written records—what about the study of natural principle?"

sentences.zh: 」他日，則又曰：「物理之學學矣，不有性命之學乎？

translations.literal: Another day he again said: "You have studied the learning of natural principle—are there not also the learning of nature and destiny?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day he again said: "You have studied the learning of natural principle—are there not also the learning of nature and destiny?"

sentences.zh: 」雍再拜，願受業，於是先示之以陸淳《春秋》，意欲以《春秋》表儀《五經》，既可語《五經》大旨，則授《易》而終焉。

translations.literal: Yong bowed twice and wished to become his disciple; thereupon he first showed him Lu Chun's Spring and Autumn Annals, intending to use the Spring and Autumn Annals as the standard for the Five Classics—once the great purport of the Five Classics could be discussed, he would transmit the Book of Changes and there end.
translations.idiomatic: Yong bowed twice and wished to become his disciple. Thereupon Zhicai first showed him Lu Chun's Spring and Autumn Annals, intending to use the Spring and Autumn Annals as the standard for the Five Classics; once the great purport of the Five Classics could be discussed, he would transmit the Book of Changes and there end.

sentences.zh: 其後雍卒以《易》名世。

translations.literal: Afterward Yong in the end became famous in the world through the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Yong came to be famous throughout the world through the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 之才器大，難乎識者，棲遲久不調。

translations.literal: Zhicai's capacity was great and hard for others to recognize; he lingered long without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai's capacity was great and hard for others to recognize; he lingered long without promotion.

sentences.zh: 或惜之，則曰：「宜少貶以圖榮進。

translations.literal: Some regretted this for him, and he would say: "One ought to lower oneself a little to seek honor and advancement."
translations.idiomatic: When some regretted this for him, he would say: "One ought to lower oneself a little to seek honor and advancement."

sentences.zh: 」石延年獨曰：「時不足以容君，盍不棄之隱去。

translations.literal: Shi Yannian alone said: "The times are not sufficient to contain you—why not abandon them and withdraw into seclusion."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yannian alone said: "The times are not sufficient to contain you—why not abandon them and withdraw into seclusion."

sentences.zh: 」再調孟州司法參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to judicial aide of Meng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to judicial aide of Meng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時範雍守孟，亦莫之知也。

translations.literal: At that time Fan Yong was administering Meng, and he too did not know of him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fan Yong was administering Meng, and he too did not know of him.

sentences.zh: 雍初自洛建節守延安，送者皆出境外，之才獨別近郊。

translations.literal: When Yong first left Luoyang with his commission to administer Yan'an, those who saw him off all went beyond the border of the prefecture; Zhicai alone took leave at the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong first left Luoyang with his commission to administer Yan'an, those who saw him off all went beyond the prefectural border; Zhicai alone took leave at the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 或病之，謝曰：「故事也。

translations.literal: Some faulted this; he apologized, saying: "It is precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Some faulted this; he apologized, saying: "It is precedent."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，雍謫安陸，之才沿檄見之洛陽，前日遠送之人無一來者，雍始恨知之之晚。

translations.literal: Before long Yong was demoted to Anlu; Zhicai, following an official dispatch, saw him in Luoyang—not one of those who had seen him off from afar the other day came; Yong only then regretted having known him so late.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yong was demoted to Anlu. Zhicai, following an official dispatch, saw him in Luoyang, and not one of those who had seen him off from afar the other day came; Yong only then regretted having known him so late.

sentences.zh: 友人尹洙以書薦於中書舍人葉道卿，因石延年致之，曰：「孟州司法參軍李之才，年三十九，能為古文章，語直意遂，不肆不窘，固足以蹈及前輩，非洙所敢品目，而安於卑位，無仕進意，人罕知之。

translations.literal: His friend Yin Shu recommended him by letter to Secretariat Drafter Ye Daoqing, conveying it through Shi Yannian, saying: "Li Zhicai, judicial aide of Meng Prefecture, aged thirty-nine, can write ancient-style prose; his language is direct and his meaning forthright, neither loose nor strained—he is certainly able to reach the level of earlier masters, not something Shu dares to rank, yet he is content in a low post with no desire for advancement, and few people know of him."
translations.idiomatic: His friend Yin Shu recommended him by letter to secretariat drafter Ye Daoqing, conveying it through Shi Yannian, saying: "Li Zhicai, judicial aide of Meng Prefecture, aged thirty-nine, can write ancient-style prose; his language is direct and his meaning forthright, neither loose nor strained—he is certainly able to reach the level of earlier masters, not something Shu dares to rank, yet he is content in a low post with no desire for advancement, and few people know of him."

sentences.zh: 其才又達世務，使少用於世，必過人遠甚，恨其貧不能決其歸心，知之者當共成之。

translations.literal: His talent also extends to worldly affairs; if he were given even a little use in the world, he would certainly far surpass others—I regret that his poverty cannot settle his heart toward service; those who know him ought together to help him succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His talent also extends to worldly affairs; if he were given even a little use in the world, he would certainly far surpass others. I regret that his poverty cannot settle his heart toward service; those who know him ought together to help him succeed.

sentences.zh: 」延年復書曰：「今業文好古之士至鮮且不張，苟遺若人，其學益衰矣。

translations.literal: Yannian replied in a further letter: "Today scholars devoted to writing and cherishing antiquity are extremely few and not promoted; if such a man is overlooked, learning will decline all the more."
translations.idiomatic: Yannian replied in a further letter: "Today scholars devoted to writing and cherishing antiquity are extremely few and not promoted; if such a man is overlooked, learning will decline all the more."

sentences.zh: 」延年素不喜謁貴仕，凡四五至道卿門，通其書乃已。

translations.literal: Yannian by nature did not like calling on the powerful; altogether four or five times he went to Daoqing's gate before the letter was delivered.
translations.idiomatic: Yannian by nature did not like calling on the powerful; altogether four or five times he went to Daoqing's gate before the letter was delivered.

sentences.zh: 道卿薦之，遂得應銓新格，有保任五人，改大理寺丞，為緱氏令。

translations.literal: Daoqing recommended him, and he was thus able to meet the new standards of the selection board, with five guarantors; he was changed to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and made magistrate of Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing recommended him, and he was thus able to meet the new standards of the selection board with five guarantors; he was made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Gou.

sentences.zh: 未行，會延年與龍圖閣直學士吳遵路調兵河東，辟之才澤州簽署判官。

translations.literal: Before he set out, it happened that Yannian and Hanlin academician on duty at the Hall of Dragon Designs Wu Zunlu were mobilizing troops in Hedong; they recruited Zhicai as signing administrator of Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, Yannian and Hanlin academician on duty at the Hall of Dragon Designs Wu Zunlu were mobilizing troops in Hedong and recruited Zhicai as signing administrator of Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 澤人劉羲叟從受曆法，世稱「羲叟曆法」，遠出古今上，有楊雄、張衡所未喻者，實之才授之。

translations.literal: Liu Xisou of Ze received calendrical methods from him; the age calls it "Xisou's calendrical methods"—far surpassing all ancient and modern times, with points Yang Xiong and Zhang Heng had not understood—and in truth it was Zhicai who taught them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xisou of Ze received calendrical methods from him; the age calls it "Xisou's calendrical methods," far surpassing all ancient and modern times, with points Yang Xiong and Zhang Heng had not understood—and in truth it was Zhicai who taught them.

sentences.zh: 在澤轉殿中丞，丁母憂，甫除喪，暴卒於懷州官舍，慶曆五年二月也。

translations.literal: While in Ze he was transferred to Palace Director; upon mourning for his mother, just as mourning ended he suddenly died at the official lodging in Huai Prefecture—in the second month of the fifth year of Qingli.
translations.idiomatic: While in Ze he was transferred to palace director. Upon mourning for his mother, just as mourning ended he suddenly died at the official lodging in Huai Prefecture—in the second month of Qingli 5.

sentences.zh: 時尹洙兄漸守懷，哭之才過哀，感疾，不逾月亦卒。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Shu's elder brother Jian was administering Huai; he mourned Zhicai with excessive grief, contracted illness, and within a month also died.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yin Shu's elder brother Jian was administering Huai; he mourned Zhicai with excessive grief, contracted illness, and within a month also died.

sentences.zh: 之才歸葬青社，邵雍表其墓，有曰：「求於天下，得聞道之君子李公以師焉。」

translations.literal: Zhicai was buried back in Qing She; Shao Yong wrote an inscription for his tomb, saying: "Seeking throughout the realm, I obtained the gentleman who had heard the Way, Master Li, to be my teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai was buried back in Qing She. Shao Yong wrote an inscription for his tomb that says: "Seeking throughout the realm, I obtained the gentleman who had heard the Way, Master Li, to be my teacher."
